new_roles.description:
**About CCNC:**

From the mountains to the coast, from large cities to small towns, Community Care of North Carolina is transforming health care. Informed by statewide data and predictive analytics, community-based care-managers work with local physicians and diverse teams of health professionals to develop whole-person plans of care that connect people to the right local resources and increase equity and access to high quality care.

**CCNC Mission Statement**

To improve the health and quality of life for all North Carolinians by building supporting better community-based healthcare delivery systems.

**Position Summary**
====================

The Director of Quality Improvement (QI) Strategy is responsible for setting the vision for the organization’s Quality Improvement strategy, in collaboration with the Population Health Division and aligned with CCNC’s mission and strategic goals. The aim of the QI strategy is to ensure the CCPN member practices deliver high - quality health care that drives successful performance of the Clinically Integrated Network (CIN).

The Director of Quality Improvement (QI) Strategy in coordination with the Clinical Performance and Practice Engagement teams, will direct, plan, implement, monitor, coordinate, and evaluate all aspects of the QI strategy and oversee daily operations to ensure that CCNC’s strategic plan is implemented. implements and informs process improvement to create standardized and streamlined processes, workflows, and education. The Director of QI Strategy provides direct supervision of the QI Specialist and the Value Based Care Program Specialist.

Responsibilities include outreach, education, training, hands-on participative leadership, and development of an increased capacity to successfully execute performance improvement across the organization. Working directly with others across the organization, The Director of Quality Improvement (QI) Strategy ensures that the elements of the QI strategy allow for coordination and collaboration of multifaceted initiatives with practices that serve our covered populations with consideration of resources, cost savings and quality. This includes providing strategic input on the development of organizational goals, to include measurement criteria and interventions for achieving the goals.

**Essential Functions**
=======================

**Operationalize QI Strategy**
------------------------------

* Direct the implementation of Quality Improvement efforts to support CCPN practices and CCNC programming in accordance with the strategic plan.
* Establish and implement the process for how PRRs utilize the QI plans to drive performance with CCPN practices.
* Facilitate the development of programs, systems, workflows, and integration efforts in alignment with CCNC and CCPN’s contractual, regulatory and quality requirements.
* Apply QI methodology, change management strategies, team facilitation, and coaching principles to achieve program effectiveness and efficiencies.
* Mentor and train on QI methodology, change management, and coaching principles (e.g. Model for Improvement, PDSA, Lean,).
* Demonstrate subject matter expertise and knowledge of payment models and their associated quality measures.
* Serve as the subject matter expert and lead for key projects and initiatives; including developing detailed work plans, assigning responsibilities, monitoring project progress and ensuring spread and sustainability.
* Assist CCPN and CCNC with future program development, creation or delegation of accountability and ownership for program roles and continuous process improvement.
* Develop annual Quality Plans with the Value Based Care Program practices in coordination with key focus areas identified by Clinical Performance.
* Represent and demonstrate our QI strategy in monthly Joint Operating Council meetings with the Value Based Care Program practices.
* Support the Practice Based Care Coordination (PBCC) program through data mining, identification of opportunities for improvement, regular practice monitoring, and ongoing training & support for the QIPS team.
* Engage and maintain collaborative relationships with the health care community, including but not limited to primary care providers, practice managers & practice team members, health departments, FQHCs and other community partners.
* Serve as Liaison on local, regional and state workgroups and collaborative efforts.
* Partner with the QI leaders for payers to establish collaborative and effective working relationships.
* Actively participate in payer meetings to represent and demonstrate our QI strategy

***Data Management, Analytics and Presentation***

* Lead QI efforts to positively impact performance and quality measures.
* Collaborate with the Clinical Performance team to use data to evaluate the effectiveness of projects across departments
* Advise leadership on project-specific data and information needs in support of staff.
* Identify areas of opportunity for CCPN practices through clinical data analysis, interpretation, & presentation.
* Lead the QI PS team to provide excellent training and support to member practices that facilitate effective use of the organization’s value-based care data platform
* In coordination with the Clinical Performance team, train on data definitions, data interpretation and data analysis
* Support all programs in achieving program goals through data analytics and quality improvement support.
* Adhere to CCNC privacy and security policies to ensure that patient and company data are properly safeguarded.

***Staff Management and Supervision***

* Provide effective leadership with respect to recruitment, selection, training, evaluation, compensation, staff development, and advocacy for the QI Strategy Team.
* Provide oversight and guidance to staff through a team approach that allows for coordinated handoffs, communication, and workflow across provider-facing staff
* Develop strategies for allocating QI resources to meet program goals and to control costs through effective use of personnel.
* Identify staff training needs and provide appropriate training opportunities.
* Complete performance evaluations.
* Utilize conflict resolution and problem-solving skills to manage issues in a timely manner.

**Qualifications**

* Registered Nurse (BSN required; MSN preferred); Social Worker (BSW required; MSW and LCSW preferred); or master's in public health or health care administration. If RN: Active, unrestricted RN license to practice in North Carolina.
* At least 5 years of Quality Improvement or relevant health care experience with responsibilities in the following areas: operational leadership, process improvement, project management, systems analysis, data analytics, and team facilitation.
* At least 3 years of supervisory or leadership experience in health care.
* NAHQ Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ)
* Lean / Six Sigma certification a plus.
* Maintain a valid NC driver’s license with current auto liability insurance.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

Excellent communication skills

* - oral, written and public speaking
* Knowledge of government, private sector and community resources
* Knowledge of and compliance with federal and state regulations applicable to the position
* Critical thinking skills, effective clinical judgment, independent decision making, and problem- solving abilities
* Skilled in establishing rapport with providers, community partners, and members
* Strong organizational and time management skills
* Demonstrated leadership skills
* Ability to work independently and function as an integral part of the team
* Expertise with Microsoft Office suite of products and comfort with database software and the internet
* Strong competence in quality improvement methodologies, principles, and recognition programs
* Ability to take “deep dives” into multiple sources of data to drive improvement
* Ability to stimulate innovative thinking & serve as a change agent
* Able to shift strategy or approach in response to the demands of a situation

**Working Conditions**

* Multiple contacts are required with providers, members, health systems and community partners to ensure effectiveness of QI and PS work; exposure to general office conditions, as well as communicable disease could occur.
* Potential for minor physical inconveniences or discomforts in the work setting, including sitting for moderate periods of time.
* Repetitive wrist motion and occasional lifting/carrying of up to 25 pounds.
* Travel required within the region and/or the state.

**Why Join Us:**
----------------

* Make a meaningful impact on youth and families across North Carolina
* Work with a supportive and collaborative care team
* Competitive Benefits Package effective first day of employment
* Opportunities for growth, training, and bonus incentives\*

**Ready to improve the health and quality of life of all North Carolinians by building and supporting better community-based health care delivery systems?**

* **Apply today and join us in delivering compassionate care that makes a difference.**

**Ready to improve the health and quality of life of all North Carolinians by building and supporting better community-based health care delivery systems?**

**Apply today** and join us in delivering compassionate care that makes a difference.

#CCNC #HealthCare #NCHealth

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Parental leave
* Professional development assistance
* Referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

new_roles.title: Director Food Safety and Quality
new_roles.description:
Job Summary
 
The Director, Food Safety & Quality is a senior, project-based individual contributor who is deployed to the most critical food safety and quality priorities across Maker’s Pride’s manufacturing network. Rather than leading a team, this leader goes where the need is greatest: stepping into facilities, programs, and issues that require immediate expertise, rapidly assessing the situation, and leading cross-functional teams to resolution without direct authority. Working in close partnership with plant leadership, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Product Development, Sanitation, and plant FSQA teams, the Director stabilizes high-risk areas, solves complex problems, and builds sustainable capability so improvements hold after the engagement ends. This role serves as a senior technical decision-maker on food safety risk and represents the company with regulators, key customers, and certification bodies on escalated matters.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 
Critical Site & Program Interventions
 

* Deploy to facilities, lines, and programs identified as highest risk or underperforming, often on short notice, to assess conditions and lead immediate stabilization.
* Rapidly diagnose root causes of food safety and quality gaps and develop clear, prioritized action plans with plant leadership.
* Lead cross-functional plant teams through execution of improvement plans, removing barriers and escalating risks as needed.
* Transition sustainable processes, tools, and ownership to site leadership before exiting each engagement.

Project Leadership & Prioritization
 

* Lead a portfolio of high-impact food safety and quality projects, defining scope, objectives, milestones, and success measures for each.
* Partner with the VP of HSE, FSQA to prioritize engagements based on enterprise risk, business impact, and customer or regulatory exposure.
* Manage multiple concurrent projects across sites, adjusting priorities quickly as new critical issues emerge.
* Provide regular project status, risk updates, and outcomes to the VP of HSE, FSQA and executive leadership.

Food Safety Risk Management & Decision-Making
 

* Serve as a senior technical decision-maker on food safety risk, including product hold, release, and disposition decisions.
* Lead or support the company’s response to food safety incidents, including recall and market withdrawal events, in partnership with senior leadership.
* Lead risk assessments and management of change reviews for high-risk changes to ingredients, processes, equipment, packaging, and facilities.
* Ensure HACCP, HARPC, and Preventive Controls programs at engaged sites are effectively designed, validated, and maintained.

**Technical Expertise:** Allergen Control, Sanitary Design & Complaints
 

* Address high-risk allergen control gaps, including labeling controls, scheduling, segregation, and cleaning validation and verification.
* Provide sanitary design expertise on critical equipment, facility, and capital projects, and ensure food safety requirements are incorporated.
* Lead investigations into significant or recurring customer and consumer complaints, driving root cause analysis and effective CAPA to closure.

External Relationships & Audit Readiness
 

* Represent Maker’s Pride with regulatory agencies, key customers, and certification bodies on escalated food safety matters.
* Lead sites through high-stakes regulatory inspections, customer audits, and GFSI-benchmarked certification audits (e.g., SQF, BRCGS), including remediation of findings.
* Support commercial teams in resolving critical customer quality concerns.

Sustainability & Network Learning
 

* Define success measures for each engagement and verify that improvements are sustained after transition.
* Capture lessons learned and translate solutions into standards, tools, and best practices that can be applied across the network.
* Identify systemic risks across engagements and recommend enterprise-level actions to prevent recurrence.

**Qualifications:** 
**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Engineering, Microbiology, Chemistry, Biological Sciences, or related discipline required.
 
 
**Experience:** 

* 10+ years of experience in food manufacturing, quality, engineering, or food safety required.
* Proven track record leading critical, high-visibility projects or turnarounds across multiple manufacturing sites required.
* Working knowledge of FSMA, HACCP, Preventive Controls, GMPs, and GFSI-benchmarked standards (SQF, BRCGS, or similar) required
* Experience with sanitary design principles and capital project support preferred
* Experience with quality management systems and data analysis tools preferred

**Certifications:** PCQI and/or HACCP certification and Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or equivalent continuous improvement certification preferred
 
 
**Skills:** 

* Strong root cause analysis and data analysis skills, with the ability to quickly assess complex, ambiguous situations and determine what matters most.
* Ability to scope, prioritize, and execute multiple concurrent projects across sites, adjusting quickly as critical issues emerge.
* Builds trust and credibility quickly with plant teams, executives, customers, and regulators to drive results with teams that do not report to them.
* Strong written and verbal communication at all levels, and comfortable shifting between sites, projects, and priorities in a high-travel role.

Work Environment & Physical Demands
 

* 70% travel to manufacturing facilities
* Work in manufacturing environments that may include exposure to noise, varying temperatures, allergens, and moving equipment.
* Ability to stand and walk for extended periods, climb stairs and ladders, and carry light loads.
* Must comply with all GMP, food safety, and safety requirements, including use of required personal protective equipment.

The information provided in this document provides an overview of the most common duties, qualifications, and demands of the position. It is not intended to be a comprehensive summary of the role, and the duties, qualifications, and demands of the position are subject to change without notice. The expectations provided here may also be modified if an employee with a disability could effectively meet the expectations for the role with reasonable accommodation.
 
The pay range for this full-time, salaried position is $141,436-$212,154/year. Individual base pay depends on work location and additional factors such as experience, job-related skills, and relevant education or training. The position is eligible for a discretionary annual incentive based on company and individual performance. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, 401k and wellness benefits beginning on the first day of employment.
 
 
Maker's Pride is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

new_roles.title: Director of Quality
new_roles.description:
Responsible to manage, promote, and continuously maintain a compliant quality management system by effectively managing the quality department that consist of validation, quality inspection, document control, change control, customer complaints, metrology, CAPA management, nonconforming product, calibration, receiving inspection and product release activities. As a quality manager you will ensure that the manufacturing site meets and applies the Global Quality Policies and Guidelines relating to, ISO 9001 & 13485 standards, FDA 21 CFR 820 regulations, customer requirements and comply with necessary local and international regulations.

**Essential Job Functions and Responsibilities****:**

* Responsible for , leading developing, implementing and manage an effective quality management systems that supports the company-wide quality policy, ISO 9000, ISO 13485 and FDA 21 CFR 820 regulations for medical devices with a continuous improvement programs.
* Lead, develop, implement and maintain quality systems for controlling product quality using process capability, inspection, auditing and statistical analysis.
* Lead, develop, implement and maintain an effective quality system for preventing nonconforming product and/or its recurrence using quality planning, material review, corrective action and quality reporting.
* Responsible for selection, interviewing and onboarding of new hires and develop a relevant training program and plan for all site personnel.
* Responsible for leading, driving and enforcing quality programs in collaboration with manufacturing team.
* Resolve customer concerns, complaints and provide feedback on quality issues.
* Analyze daily and monthly quality reports and develop tests to improve product quality.
* Manage day to day department activities.
* Support company quality policy and objectives.
* Ensure products produced meets customer expectations (approve quality specifications) and regulatory requirements
* Lead customer audits, ISO audits and Internal audits
* Achieve financial objectives (maintain department salaries within budget, prepare the Quality budget, schedule the expenditures)
* Follow and report of the site quality performances from a quality standpoint and ensure alignment with Business Unit and manage continuous improvement for product quality
* In cooperation with the Sites Quality Coordinator, develop and implement Quality Objectives in line with objectives of the business unit
* Lead and influence a quality mindset to quality and operations to maintain, improving and maintaining quality system requirements.
* Continually improve quality through analyzing, identifying, and eliminating root causes. Such improvements include reducing defects, decreasing scrap, reducing waste, and improving outputs.
* Apply and evaluate testing and inspection methods; including the identification of requirements for improvements.
* Develop and implement quality cost reduction concepts and techniques.
* Manage department resources, including work assignments, training, cross training, personnel issues, hiring decisions, performance appraisals, motivation, efficiency, capacity and accuracy of work.
* Ensure shift-to-shift communication.
* Provide a safe work environment and resolve any safety issues that arise.
* Perform other job-related duties as assigned.

**Core Competencies:**

* Facilitation
* Conflict Management
* Fostering Learning
* Information Gathering & Processing
* Interactive Communication
* Partnering
* Relationship Building
* Research
* Teamwork
* Writing Skills
* Attention to detail
* Adaptability
* Concern for Safety
* Proactive and self-motivated
* Strong time management with priority setting skills
* Client focused

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Expert knowledge and interpretation of ISO 13485, ISO 9000 standards, 21 CFR 820 and cGMP compliance.
* Ability to lead, implement quality management systems as applicable to ISO and 21 CFR regulations.
* Demonstrate understanding of industry standard validation tools and techniques.
* Demonstrated ability of metrology and basic inspection tools, metrology and injection molding workmanship standards.
* Ability to develop/conduct quality related training programs.
* Effectively communicate in both verbal and written.
* Good organizational skills.
* Excellent English communication skills (both written and verbal).
* Fluency in Spanish a plus.
* Understanding and use of metrology equipment.
* Ability to read drawings and good understanding of geometric tolerancing.
* Knowledge of processing engineering polymers is a plus.
* Exceptional leadership skills which include ability to prioritize, lead, direct, train, and motivate staff.
* Ability to influence peers.
* Excellent planning and organizational skills.
* Good analytical, problem-solving and math skills. Six Sigma and Lean knowledge a plus.
* Understanding and use of sampling plans, Gauge R&R, statistical techniques and SPC.
* Ability to use personal computer and Windows-based software (Outlook, Word and Excel preferred). Use of PC-DMIS metrology software, IQMS manufacturing software and Minitab a plus.

**Education and/or Experience**:

* Bachelor’s degree desirable, four-year college degree (preferably in a sciences chemical, pharmacy, plastics or engineering field) or equivalent combined college/work experience.
* At least 5 years of leading and implementing quality systems in a pharmaceutical or medical device environment
* Manufacturing experience in injection molding plastics industry (or equivalent industry) is a plus.

new_roles.title: Director of Quality
new_roles.description:
Harvest Solar, an equal opportunity employer, is a Michigan-based company that provides cost-effective renewable energy for agriculture, commercial, and utility customers yielding more energy independence by utilizing solar energy. We believe in energy independence and a sustainable future for our children and grandchildren. Our purpose is to empower people to create and use renewable energy by providing them with the best‐in‐class service, products, and experience. 
 
**Position Title and Purpose of Position** 
The Director of Quality will develop, coordinate, and implement quality and commissioning policies and procedures to ensure safe, efficient, and compliant operations throughout the organization. The Director of Quality is responsible for site specific quality and commissioning compliance within both Harvest’s and the customer’s requirements. The Director of Quality will work closely with onsite Harvest Solar project management, direct-labor staff, customer’s representatives, and subcontractors to ensure all work is completed to established requirements.

**Salary** 
The salary range for this role is $110,000.00 to $130,000.00 USD, salary commensurate with education and experience. An Annual Bonus Target representing 10% of your annual base salary/annual wages is paid based on meeting both organizational and individual targets. 
 
**Major Responsibilities of Position**

* Ensure a “Safe Culture” through employee engagement, training, coaching, and compliance
* Responsible for planning, developing, implementing, maintaining, and improving quality and commissioning policies and procedures in compliance with Harvest requirements along with customer, Utility, and AHJ requirements
* Responsible for planning, developing, implementing, and providing quality and commissioning training for relevant employees
* Identifies opportunities to improve existing policies and procedures
* Maintain quality and commissioning records using Procore and other customer required systems
* Prepare written reports of findings and recommendations for corrective or preventive measures where indicated; follow up to ensure measures have been implemented
* Work with project management teams and field workers to implement solutions to quality issues on project sites
* Provide technical support to Preconstruction department for quoting and proposals
* Represent company in meetings with governing bodies (AHJ, utilities), subcontractors, and customer on issues regarding quality and commissioning
* Responsible for managing direct reports
* Other duties as assigned

The successful candidate will have: (Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Other Attributes)

* Ability to read, analyze, and interpret general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations.
* Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals.
* Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from managers, clients, employees, and the public
* Ability to prioritize tasks especially when handling an accident or incident
* Ability to manage daily priorities and ensure task accomplishment
* Ability to communicate effectively, both oral and written
* Thorough knowledge of health and safety laws and guidelines
* Extensive attention to detail to distinguish safety hazards
* Good understanding of data analysis and risk assessment
* Good organizational, leadership and motivational skills
* Maintain regular and acceptable attendance
* Willing to work hours necessary to support the accomplishment of organizational goals

**Educational and Certification Background**

* High school diploma or GED – Required.
* Bachelor’s degree in safety management and five years’ experience; or ten years’ experience coordinating safety & environmental programs; experience in construction environment preferred.
* Valid State Driver’s License – Required
* OSHA 30 - Preferred
* MIOSHA Level I or Level II Certification, or OHSA 500 - Preferred

**Work Environment**

* Commercial Construction Setting 20% of the time: Job Site terrain and outdoor work with exposure to weather fluctuations in addition to construction site hazards. Installers travel to work sites and therefore, travel is required 100% of the time. Harvest values our employees work life balance and whenever possible, overnight travel is Monday through Friday. Hotel and transportations costs are covered. Additionally, a food per diem is paid for overnight stays.
* Travel Required 20% of the time: Position supports job site activities therefore daily and overnight travel is required. Harvest values our employees work life balance and whenever possible, overnight travel is Monday through Friday. Hotel and transportations costs are covered. Additionally, per diem is paid for overnight stays.

**Benefit Offerings** 
 
**Immediately after Hire:**

* Nine Paid Holidays per Year. Including: New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Day after Thanksgiving, and Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Years Eve.
* Paid Vacation: Vacation time is accrued each week at a rate of .924 to achieve 48 hours in the calendar year. Unused vacation can be paid out and/or up to 40 unused hours can be rolled over at year end.
* Paid Time Off (PTO): 72 Hours are available each year on January 1. In the first year of employment available hours are prorated based on your date of hire.

**The First of the Month after the Date of Hire**:

* Health Insurance. The premiums are a shared expense with 80% covered by Harvest Solar and 20% covered by the associate via a weekly payroll deduction. Premiums are based on level of coverage, (i.e., Associate only, Associate & Spouse, Associate & Child(ren), Family).
 + Option 1: Priority Health, HMO HSA 2000 Plan
 + Members must seek care from in-network providers.
 + HSA compatible health plan. An HSA is a tax-deductible savings account used in conjunction with the health plan. Contribution limits are determined by the IRS. Harvest Solar will make the following weekly deposit into your HSA account based on the coverage options: Associate: $10.64; Associate & Spouse: $27.25; Associate & Child(ren): $21.65; Family: $37.55
* Option 2: Priority Health, Traditional HMO 1000 Plan
 + Members must seek care from in-network providers.
 + Preventive care covered 100% when received in-network.
 + Not an HSA compatible health plan.
* Dental Insurance The premiums are a shared expense with 80% covered by Harvest Solar and 20% covered by the associate via a weekly payroll deduction.
* Vision Insurance: The premiums are a shared expense with 80% covered by Harvest Solar and 20% covered by the associate via a weekly payroll deduction.
* Group Life Insurance: $50,000.00 of group life insurance, with and Accident Death clause. Premiums are covered by Harvest Solar
* Group Short Term Disability: 60% of your earnings, with a $1,000.00 weekly maximum, are available for injury or illness after a seven-day waiting period. Premiums are covered by Harvest Solar.
* Voluntary Supplemental Programs: Accident, Critical illness, and Hospital Indemnity are available at the associate’s expense. Plans are organized through Allstate and premiums are paid through payroll deduction.

**The First of the Month After 90-Days of Employment:**

* Harvest Solar 401k Plan: Associates are auto enrolled at a 3% deferral rate. Once enrolled, the associate may make changes that include:
 + Increasing the Deferral Rate to the Applicable IRS Limits: A company match is available. When the associate defers 3%, Harvest Solar matches 3%. When the associate defers 4%, Harvest Solar matches 3.5%. When the associate defers 5%, Harvest Solar matches 4%.

new_roles.title: Director, Quality Engineering
new_roles.description:
HHAeXchange is the leading technology platform for home and community-based care. Founded in 2008, HHAeXchange was born out of an idea to create a fully comprehensive end-to-end homecare solution to help people who are aging or have disabilities thrive in their homes and communities. Our employees are passionate about transforming the healthcare space by building the only homecare ecosystem that fully connects patients, personal care providers, managed care organizations, and states.

The Director, Quality Engineering will lead the enterprise-wide quality strategy and Quality Assurance (QA) program across HHAeXchange. This role is responsible for standardizing testing processes and tools, driving test automation, and ensuring our products meet high standards for reliability, performance, security, and accessibility. The Director, Quality Engineering will oversee functional and non-functional testing practices, including accessibility (WCAG) and security-related validation, and will own processes that support customer User Acceptance Testing (UAT).

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential job duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**This is a fully remote opportunity for candidates located in the EST or CST time zones within the US only.**

### **Essential Job Duties**

* **Enterprise Quality Leadership:** Develop, implement, and lead the overall quality strategy and QA operating model across the organization.
* **Standardize Testing Processes:** Define and enforce consistent testing approaches including test planning, test cases, regression strategy, and release readiness criteria.
* **Tooling Ownership:** Select, implement, and manage enterprise testing tools for test management, automation, performance, accessibility, and security validation.
* **Automation Strategy:** Drive increased automated test coverage across UI, API, mobile, and services, reducing reliance on manual regression testing.
* **Compliance, Accessibility & VPAT Reporting:**
 + Lead accessibility testing programs aligned to WCAG 2.1+
 + Oversee creation and maintenance of Voluntary Product Accessibility Templates (VPATs) and Accessibility Conformance Reports
 + Partner with Product, Legal, and Compliance to respond to customer accessibility requirements and audits
* **Security & Compliance Testing Support:** Coordinate with Security teams on SAST/DAST, vulnerability validation, and remediation tracking.
* **Customer UAT Support:**
 + Define and support customer UAT strategies and environments
 + Provide test plans, data guidance, and defect triage support during customer acceptance testing cycles
 + Ensure feedback from UAT informs release decisions and product quality improvements
* **Quality Metrics & Reporting:** Establish KPIs to measure product quality, defect escape rate, automation coverage, UAT outcomes, and release readiness; communicate results to leadership.
* **Shift-Left Quality Practices:** Embed quality earlier in the development lifecycle through collaboration on requirements, acceptance criteria, and CI/CD integration.
* **Incident & Defect Management:** Oversee defect triage for high-priority production and pre-production issues and ensure timely resolution and root-cause prevention.
* **Cross-Functional Collaboration:** Work closely with Product Management, Engineering, DevOps, Security, and Compliance to ensure alignment of quality practices across releases.
* **Organizational Leadership**: Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team of QA engineers, SDETs, automation engineers, and accessibility/compliance testers.
* **Continuous Improvement:** Identify quality gaps and drive process improvements that improve product reliability, reduce rework, and increase delivery confidence.
* **Release Governance:** Participate in release readiness reviews and serve as a key stakeholder in go/no-go decisions.

new_roles.title: DIRECTOR OF QUALITY & COMPLIANCE
new_roles.description:
**Director of Quality & Compliance**
====================================

**Southern Peaks, Canon City CO**

[Full-Time)

$95,000 To $120,000 Annually

DailyPay Available

**Looking for More Than Just a Job?**
-------------------------------------

At Abraxaswe believe every person deserves the opportunity to live a meaningful, fulfilling, and independent life.

We’re seeking compassionate, dedicated professionals who are looking for more than a paycheck. We’re looking for individuals who want to make a difference, build rewarding careers, and become part of a team committed to helping others succeed.

Whether you’re beginning your career, changing professions, or bringing years of experience, we provide the training, support, and opportunities needed to help you thrive.

**About Abraxas**
-----------------

For more than 50 years, Abraxas has been dedicated to improving lives through high-quality services and support.

Our employees play a vital role in helping individuals achieve greater independence, confidence, and success while promoting dignity, respect, inclusion, and personal choice.

Every day, our team members make a meaningful impact by supporting people in reaching their goals and living their best lives.

**Why Join Our Team?**
======================

**Competitive Pay & Benefits**
------------------------------

* Competitive Compensation
* DailyPay – Access Your Earned Wages Before Payday
* Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance- AFTER 30 DAYS
* 401(k) Retirement Plan
* Paid Time Off
* Employee Assistance Program
* Wellness Programs
* Employee Referral Bonuses
* Company-Paid Training

**Career Growth & Development**
-------------------------------

* Paid Training Programs
* Professional Development Opportunities
* Certification Opportunities
* Leadership Development Programs
* Career Advancement Opportunities
* Opportunities Across Multiple Service Lines

**Meaningful Work That Matters**
--------------------------------

* Make a Difference Every Day
* Support Individuals and Families
* Build Meaningful Relationships
* Strengthen Communities
* Join a Mission-Driven Organization

**What You’ll Do**
==================

As the Director of Quality & Compliance, you will:

Oversees compliance with applicable Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS) Volume 7 residential licensing rules, including 12 CCR 2509-8, Section 7.714, as well as payer contracts and Joint Commission standards.

* Reviews and approves corrective action plans for regulatory, payer, and accreditation findings before routing them for final approval. Verifies implementation and sustained compliance.
* Works with Quality and Compliance Specialist and Program Directors to prepare for licensing inspections, Medicaid and managed care reviews, and accreditation surveys.
* Serves as a compliance liaison with CDHS and applicable Regional Accountable Entities (RAEs) and other payers. Reviews provider manuals and contract changes and translates requirements into program procedures.
* Conducts program and follow-up audits, including reviews of admissions, assessments, treatment plans, service documentation, discharge planning, and continuity of care.
* Provides technical assistance to Quality and Compliance Specialists and trains program staff on licensing, payer, and accreditation requirements.
* Develops monitoring tools with Quality and Compliance Specialists to verify compliance and consistent implementation of program policies.
* Analyzes audit findings, incidents, grievances, clinical outcomes, and authorization or denial trends. Reports findings and tracks improvement actions with program leaders.
* Partners with Clinical, Admissions, and Billing to oversee utilization management, including prior authorization, concurrent and continued-stay review, medical necessity and level-of-care documentation, and responses to denials and appeals.
* Develops and reviews policies and procedures, supports the annual review process, and verifies that programs maintain current policy and procedure manuals.
* Participates on various internal and external committees as needed.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**Who We’re Looking For**
=========================

You may be a great fit if you are:

✔ Compassionate

✔ Dependable

✔ Patient

✔ Team-Oriented

✔ Service-Focused

✔ Professional

✔ Positive

✔ Committed to Helping Others

**Qualifications**
==================

Master's degree in social sciences, healthcare or related field and five years of quality and compliance experience or bachelor’s degree in social sciences, healthcare or related field and seven years quality and compliance experience

* Ability to effectively supervise employees.
* Extensive hands-on experience with Colorado Volume 7 residential licensing requirements, Health First Colorado behavioral health managed care, and applicable accreditation standards is critical.
* Ability to interpret and teach the application of regulations, payer requirements, accreditation standards, and contractual language.
* Experience with behavioral health utilization management, including authorization, medical necessity and continued-stay documentation, and payer audits. Experience in youth residential mental health or psychiatric residential treatment facilities (PRTFs) is preferred.
* Experience with Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA) compliance, including staff training, audit preparation, and corrective action follow-up, is preferred.
* Knowledge of adolescent residential mental health treatment, including trauma-informed care, co-occurring conditions, and the needs of youth involved in child welfare or juvenile justice.
* Proven ability to develop and revise policies that meet licensing, payer, contractual, and accreditation requirements.
* Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in written form, with a diverse group of people including regulatory agency representatives, employees, clients, governing body members, and the general public.
* Must be available for travel, to include overnight stays.
* Must have a valid driver’s license.
* Ability to work with computers and the necessary software typically used by the department.

**Physical Requirements (If Applicable)**
=========================================

* Ability to lift up to 25 pounds
* Ability to stand, walk, bend, and assist individuals as needed
* Ability to perform essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation

**Apply Today**
===============

Some jobs pay the bills. Some jobs build careers. This job changes lives.

If you’re looking for meaningful work where your compassion, dedication, and hard work make a real difference every day, we encourage you to apply today.

**Join our team and become the reason someone has a better day.**

### **About Our Organization**

**Abraxas** is part of the Inperium family of companies.

Employment for this position is administered through Apis Services, Inc.

### **Equal Opportunity Employer**

Apis Services, Inc., Inperium Inc., and affiliates provide equal employment opportunities for all employees and applicants for employment in compliance with all federal and applicable state and local laws and regulations, including nondiscrimination in hiring and employment.

All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, genetic information, marital status, pregnancy, childbirth, veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

This policy of nondiscrimination and equal employment opportunity extends to every phase and aspect of hiring and employment

new_roles.title: Southwest Regional Director of Production and Logistics
new_roles.description:
About PopUp Bagels

PopUp Bagels is not just a bagel company—we’re a cultural movement. Our stores are small, our vibes are loud, and our energy is contagious. From signature neon and iconic bullhorns to our “Not Famous but Known” mirror, we’ve reimagined not just how a bagel is created, but how it’s enjoyed: Grip, Rip and Dip! With a cult-like following, massive social presence, and unparalleled collaborations with top companies, partners and Brand Ambassadors PopUp Bagels is defining a new food lifestyle brand.

We keep things simple, but we do them really, really well. And our customers agree.

The Role

We're looking for a Regional Director to lead operations at our Nevada cream cheese production facility. This facility will play an important role in supporting PopUp's continued growth and our ability to deliver the products our customers love.

This is a senior operational leadership role responsible for overseeing the day-to-day performance of the facility, from the moment raw materials come through the door to the second finished goods ship out to shops around the country.

Here's what makes this role different from other operations roles: we're building something big, and we're building quickly. With established production facilities and operating procedures already in place, the right person for this role will know how to take proven processes, put them into practice, and continue improving them as we grow.

We're looking for a problem-solver who isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves and find solutions, a leader who earns trust on the floor just as easily as they collaborate with senior leadership, and someone who can translate operational expectations into consistent, measurable results.

This role serves as a key connection between the Nevada production facility and our broader operations leadership team. You'll have the opportunity to influence how we operate, develop our people, and contribute to the continued evolution of our production processes as PopUp expands.

If you're a driven leader who thrives in fast-moving environments, values collaboration, and takes pride in building strong teams and efficient operations, this could be the role for you.

What You'll Do:

Run the Facility. You'll provide day-to-day operational leadership and oversight across Cream Cheese and Schmear production, Warehouse, Quality Assurance, Sanitation, and Equipment Maintenance Working closely with the President of Operations and other facility leaders, you'll implement and maintain established SOPs, manage production schedules, drive throughput targets, and identify opportunities to continuously improve how we operate. You'll be responsible for addressing operational challenges, escalating significant issues when appropriate, and ensuring the facility consistently meets established performance, quality, and safety expectations.

Lead People Who Make an Impact. Building a strong team culture is at the core of this role. You'll recruit, develop, and retain a workforce that makes a genuine impact at PopUp Bagels. You'll coach and support your management team, reinforce established training programs, and identify opportunities to strengthen employee development as the operation grows. You'll create an environment where accountability and recognition go hand in hand. Our hourly workforce is the backbone of this operation, and how you show up for them defines everything.

Manage the Numbers. You'll be accountable for facility-level operational performance, including production costs, labor efficiency, waste reduction, and budget adherence. You'll partner closely with the President of Operations, Finance, and Accounting on budgeting, forecasting, and period-end reporting, and regularly communicate facility performance, challenges, and opportunities to senior leadership. You'll identify ways to improve efficiency and control costs without compromising quality, safety, or people, while supporting broader capital planning and investment decisions.

Drive Supply Chain Alignment. Work directly with our VP of Supply Chain to align production schedules with material availability. You'll oversee raw material procurement planning, inventory controls, and warehouse operations, ensuring established FIFO and food safety standards are consistently followed. You'll collaborate with Supply Chain and other production facilities to support inventory accuracy, product availability, and efficient distribution.

Lead Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance. Champion a food-safety-first culture across every part of the facility. You'll ensure consistent execution of established food safety programs and compliance with applicable FDA regulations, FSMA requirements, HACCP plans, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC), as applicable. You'll partner with Quality Assurance and the President of Operations to maintain rigorous in-process and finished product quality standards, address compliance concerns, and implement corrective actions when something doesn't meet the bar.

Collaborate Across the Company. You'll represent Nevada facility operations in company-wide leadership meetings and collaborate with Distribution & Logistics, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and corporate leadership. You'll translate what's happening on the floor into meaningful operational insights, communicate opportunities for improvement, and ensure company priorities and decisions are effectively implemented at the facility level.

Who You Are and What You Bring

We're looking for a leader who is genuinely:

A scrappy problem-solver. When something breaks at 7am or a key ingredient is backordered, you find a way. You're resourceful, calm under pressure, and put in the time to figure it out. You know when to make decisions, when to collaborate, and when to escalate an issue.

A trust-builder. Your team respects you because you've worked to build trust, not because of your title. You're on the floor, you know people's names, and you follow through on what you say.

A galvanizing leader. You provide clear direction, get buy-in, and bring your team along with energy and conviction. People want to work hard for you because they know you'll do the same for them.

Equally at home in a leadership meeting and a production room. You can review financial and operational performance in the morning and troubleshoot a production issue in the afternoon. You don't ask your team to do what you're not willing to do yourself.

Built for growth and continuous improvement. PopUp is growing fast, and our processes will continue to evolve. You appreciate the value of established systems and standards, but you're also comfortable identifying opportunities to make them better. You know how to balance consistency with adaptability as the business scales.

You bring:

* Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Master's degree (MBA or MS) preferred.
* 8–10+ years of progressive plant or manufacturing operations leadership experience, including demonstrated responsibility for facility performance, team leadership, and operational budgets.
* Experience leading operations in fast-paced manufacturing environments, preferably within growing or multi-site organizations.
* Proven track record of leading high-performing, cross-functional manufacturing teams.
* Prior food and beverage industry experience strongly preferred; dairy, cream cheese, spreads, or related refrigerated food production experience is a significant plus.
* Familiarity with food safety regulatory frameworks, including FSMA, HACCP, GMP, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC, AIB).
* Strong financial acumen, including budget management, cost analysis, labor efficiency, and operational performance reporting.
* Working knowledge of production cost drivers, manufacturing KPIs, and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Production Excellence, or equivalent).
* Demonstrated experience implementing and maintaining standardized operating procedures, production processes, and operational controls.
* Experience partnering with corporate Finance, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and Distribution teams.
* Availability and willingness to be on-call on weekends and off-hours to respond to facility disruptions or emergencies.
* Experience supporting capital improvement projects and operational efficiency initiatives.
* A history of building positive, rewarding workplace cultures for hourly workforces.

Physical Requirements

The following physical requirements are representative of those needed to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with qualifying disabilities.

* Ability to walk, stand, and move throughout a production facility for extended periods during daily floor presence and inspections.
* Must be able to work in a manufacturing environment with varying temperatures, including refrigerated dairy production and storage areas, moderate to loud noise levels, and exposure to dairy ingredients and food-grade cleaning agents.
* Occasional lifting of up to 50 pounds may be required.
* Must be able to wear required PPE, including hair nets, beard nets, gloves, and safety footwear when on the production floor.
* Ability to use standard office equipment (computer, monitor, phone, conferencing technology) for extended periods.
* Occasional travel to corporate offices, other production facilities, or external meetings (estimated up to 30%).

PopUp Bagels is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We do not discriminate based on race, age, ancestry, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, pregnancy, childbirth or related condition, unemployment status, gender identity or expression, transgender status, marital status, domestic violence or sexual violence victim status, national origin, citizenship, disability, covered veteran and/or military status, genetic information, familial status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, and local law. PopUp Bagels conducts pre-employment screenings in compliance with local, state, and federal laws, and utilizes E-Verify to confirm U.S. employment eligibility.

The duties of this position may change from time to time. PopUp Bagels reserves the right to add or delete duties and responsibilities at its discretion. This posting describes the general nature and level of work expected and is not intended to be all-inclusive.

new_roles.title: VP of Operations & Supply Chain
new_roles.description:
**Position Overview**

The Vice President of Operations & Supply Chain serves as an executive operational leader responsible for driving domestic manufacturing performance while scaling global strategic sourcing. Headquartered on-site at our metal fabrication and assembly facility, this role oversees domestic plant operations and integrates supply chain operations within a focused portfolio of key international suppliers. This leader will balance hands-on, plant-level operational leadership with high-level international sourcing strategy to support business growth.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Domestic Manufacturing & Plant Operations**

· Lead all daily plant operations across metal fabrication, assembly, quality control, safety, and inventory management.

· Drive continuous improvement (Lean / Six Sigma) to optimize throughput, reduce scrap rates, and manage labor efficiency.

· Foster a high-accountability safety culture adhering to OSHA standards.

· Maintain direct, visible leadership on the shop floor to build strong relationships with operational teams.

· Establish clear key performance indicators (KPIs) for manufacturing efficiency, operational costs, equipment utilization, and schedule adherence.

· Oversee capital expenditure (CapEx) planning, facility maintenance, and automation/equipment upgrades to optimize plant capacity and throughput.

**2. Global Supply Chain, Strategic Sourcing & Post-Acquisition Integration**

· Partner with executive business leaders to architect and execute a unified global supply chain strategy leveraging domestic fabrication alongside overseas contract manufacturing partners.

· Align and execute global supply chain initiatives to support these activities, blending distinct business models (domestic fabrication vs. Asian contract manufacturing).

· Establish vendor management systems, quality standards, and logistics frameworks for international contract manufacturers.

· Develop processes to manage import/export compliance, international logistics, tariffs, and total landed cost models.

· Evaluate and optimize global supplier networks to build resilience, optimize costs, and drive margin performance.

· Establish end-to-end supply chain visibility and inventory positioning strategies across domestic warehouses and overseas vendor pipelines

**3. Industry Alignment & Custom Project Delivery**

· Align manufacturing capacity and scheduling with the fast-paced, custom-project demand cycles typical of the hospitality furnishings/fixtures market.

· Partner with Sales, Engineering, and Project Management to deliver custom fabricated assemblies on time and within budget.

**4. Executive Leadership & Culture**

· Serve as a core member of the operational leadership team, aligning operational goals with company-wide profitability and growth targets.

· Lead with a general management orientation—translating financial targets into shop-floor operational realities.

· Thrive as a key community and company leader in a small-town operational setting.

**Candidate Qualifications**

· **Experience:** 15+ years of progressive leadership in manufacturing operations and supply chain management.

· **Industry Background:** Proven background in metal fabrication, welding, stamping, and assembly—ideally serving the hospitality, commercial interiors, or custom project-based industries.

· **Global Experience:** Demonstrated experience with international sourcing, managing Asian contract manufacturers, and post-merger supply chain integration.

· **Company Size Fit:** Experience operating in mid-market environment ($50M–$150M revenue) with 200+ employees; comfortable wearing multiple hats without heavy administrative infrastructure.

· **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in operations management and/or Supply Chain Management (Master’s / MBA preferred).

**Key Attributes & Fit Factors**

· **Dual-Oriented Leadership:** Ability to walk the factory floor in work boots in the morning and lead strategic global supplier negotiations in the afternoon.

· **Cultural & Community Fit:** Comfortable living and leading in a small-town environment while maintaining a broad, global perspective.

· **Change Management:** Skilled in bridging two distinct operational cultures—domestic manufacturing and international third-party sourcing.

Pay: $76,800.00 - $92,600.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Disability insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

new_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**Job Summary**

The Director of Manufacturing will provide strategic and operational leadership across manufacturing operations, ensuring production performance, scalability, operational excellence, cost efficiency, and quality. This role is responsible for developing manufacturing strategies, leading cross-functional teams, and aligning operations with business growth and organizational objectives.

**Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with organizational goals.
* Lead manufacturing operations, production, and operational support functions.
* Establish operational KPIs and drive accountability across manufacturing teams.
* Improve production capacity, throughput, efficiency, quality, and cost performance.
* Lead continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.
* Develop and implement workforce planning and organizational strategies.
* Collaborate with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, and leadership.
* Support new product introduction, process transfers, and manufacturing scale-up.
* Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, quality, and safety requirements.
* Develop management teams and succession planning.
* Identify opportunities for automation, technology implementation, and process innovation.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, or related field.
* 10+ years of manufacturing experience.
* 5+ years of senior manufacturing leadership experience.
* Proven experience managing complex manufacturing operations.
* Strong background in operational excellence, Lean, Six Sigma, or process improvement.
* Experience managing budgets, KPIs, production capacity, and large teams.
* Experience in medical devices, biotech, aerospace, electronics, or advanced manufacturing preferred.

new_roles.title: Director, Global Supply Chain Center of Excellence – Chemical Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**The Opportunity:**
--------------------

**Position purpose**

 
 

Lead the global Supply Chain Center of Excellence across three pillars: Planning Excellence & Governance; Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement; and Data, Systems & Digital Enablement.

 
 

Strengthen supply chain performance by establishing consistent planning practices, delivering actionable analysis and measurable improvements, and enabling reliable data and effective planning technology. Partner with regional supply chain leaders to build capabilities and sustain improvements while regional teams retain operational supply and inventory accountability.

 
 

**How you will thrive and create an impact**

 

**Planning Excellence & Governance**

* Establish global planning standards, business rules, decision rights, and exception thresholds.
* Define planning horizons, freeze rules, and handoffs between master supply planning, site scheduling, materials planning, and regional supply planning.
* Own S&OE/S&OP process design, calendars, review standards, and escalation methods.
* Establish Plan for Every Part (PFEP) standards and review methods for finished goods, raw materials, and packaging.
* Assess planning-process adoption and effectiveness, identify gaps, and lead improvements with regional owners.
* Build planner capabilities through training, coaching, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

**Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement**

* Establish common KPIs, dashboards, and performance-analysis methods across regions.
* Lead capacity scenarios and inventory modeling to support supply, working-capital, and investment decisions.
* Develop inventory policies, safety-stock methods, and replenishment recommendations with regional teams.
* Partner with Manufacturing and regional planning teams to improve capacity utilization, campaign planning, and planning parameters.
* Identify and quantify value leakage, including excess inventory, expiry, write-offs, premium freight, and avoidable expediting.
* Develop prioritized improvement initiatives with clear business cases, accountable execution owners, and milestones.
* Track corrective actions and validate realized benefits with Finance, distinguishing recurring savings, cash release, and cost avoidance.

**Data, Systems & Digital Enablement**

* Establish master-data standards, business ownership, validation controls, and data-quality remediation processes.
* Prioritize SAP planning gaps and configuration issues and lead business resolution with IT.
* Lead the business workstream for planning system implementation and SAP integration, including requirements, data readiness, testing, and deployment readiness.
* Advance reporting and workflow automation to improve planning productivity and exception management.
* Develop AI-enabled reporting, exception insights, and commentary with appropriate validation and accountable business review.

new_roles.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53229
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring a Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations for our new highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and rigor. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations owns cross-suite production performance across upstream and downstream operations in both single-use and stainless-steel suites. As the site scales to six suites, this leader is accountable for delivery of the site production plan, manufacturing cost performance, and workforce strategy, drives daily operational discipline through MDI and lean standard work, and represents manufacturing on the site Leadership Team.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Own cross-suite production performance and site-wide annual batch plan attainment across all operating suites

* Lead fully integrated, operations-focused suite teams, with upstream, downstream, and support activities managed within each suite, and clear day-to-day accountability for execution, staffing, and scheduling

* Oversee these functions OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary responsible party for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Champion adoption of lean principles across manufacturing including standardized work, visual controls, and a culture of continuous improvement (kaizen) as the site scales to six suites

* Lead the production plan across all suites, working with supply chain to align the supply plan to the production schedule through the site S&OP process

* Drive the site's daily MFG MDI process at the suite level surfacing, escalating, and resolving issues in real time across all shifts

* Serve as the manufacturing process and cost owner, driving cost-per-batch performance and contributing to the site Annual Operating Plan (AOP) and budget

* Manage workforce strategy and ramp for the manufacturing organization, including multi-shift staffing, hiring, training, and qualification of operators as new suites come online

* Ensure cGMP compliance, right-first-time execution, and inspection readiness on the manufacturing floor, partnering closely with Quality on deviations and batch record performance

* Champion a zero-harm EHS culture and drive manufacturing safety performance across all shifts

* Lead manufacturing operational readiness for suites entering service, partnering with Technical Services on tech transfer, process readiness, and PPQ execution

* Build and maintain a lean, scalable manufacturing organization, including area management and round-the-clock shift coverage within each suite

* Partner with quality, technical services, supply chain, environmental health & safety, and operational excellence to resolve issues quickly and operate as one aligned site leadership team

* Establish high standards for performance management and accountability; develop and retain talent; perform other duties as required

* Own a gross margin improvement program and goal for this function, contributing to the site's overall margin performance
 

 

**This role requires****:**

* B.S in engineering, life sciences, or a related technical field
 + Sr. Director: 15+ years in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including large-molecule drug substance operations including 7+ years of progressive leadership
 + Executive Director: 18+ years in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including large-molecule drug substance operations including 7+ years of progressive leadership
 + Level will be determined based on experience
* Financially literate, with demonstrated experience of delivering production plan attainment, managing cost per batch, and operating within an annual budget

* Experience leading the start-up and ramp of manufacturing suites or facilities

* Experience leading large, multi-shift GMP organizations and building leadership depth

* Previous people leadership/supervisory experience

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.

Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.

 
 

Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

The purpose of such checks is to verify certain information prior to the commencement of employment such as identity, right to work and educational qualifications.

 
 

For jobs in Canada: this posting is for an existing position.

new_roles.title: Director of Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement
new_roles.description:
The Director of Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement is the company's technical authority for how meals are made and the owner of its improvement engine. This hands-on leader combines deep manufacturing process engineering with a disciplined continuous improvement approach to make production operations more consistent, efficient, safe, and cost-effective across Mom's Meals.

The role will focus primarily on kitchen and production operations, supporting a highly automated manufacturing environment through process design, equipment performance, root cause problem solving, and structured improvement projects. The position will also support fulfillment operations by identifying automation and process opportunities that improve throughput, labor efficiency, accuracy, and customer service.

The Director partners closely with Production, Fulfillment, Supply Chain, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance, R&D, IT, and Finance to execute strategic projects and deliver measurable, sustained improvement across the enterprise. This is a player-coach role: the Director is expected to engage directly on the production floor, lead technical problem solving, and develop the engineers and improvement practitioners on the team.

***This position will travel to our other facilities 25-50% at varying times.***

***Ideally, the selected candidate will work out of one of our Production facilities (Ankeny/Grinnell, IA, Oklahoma City, OK, or North Jackson, OH) but are open to remote for the right skills and experience.***

Benefits

Our employees enjoy a generous package of benefits that we are thrilled to provide, and feel is part of what makes us different as an employer. We value our team members, and this is one way we can show it.

Benefits include:

* PTO, holiday pay and holiday of choice

* 401(k) match

* Life insurance

* Short-term disability

* Health, dental and vision insurance

* Maternity/paternity leave

* Health savings account (HSA)

* Flex spending accounts (FSA) – health and dependent

### **Position Responsibilities may include, but not limited to**

Process & Technical Engineering

* Serve as the company's process authority for meal production, owning process design, line layouts, standard work, and process specifications for cooking, chilling, portioning, and packaging
* Lead structured process control plans, risk assessments, and capability studies to reduce variation and improve consistency
* Drive yield, discard, and portion-control improvements through engineering-based solutions
* Partner with Production, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance and R&D teams to ensure process changes are validated, documented, and sustained on the production floor
* Reduce downtime and defects through root cause analysis and hands-on, engineering-based problem solving
* Evaluate emerging manufacturing technologies and process innovations that improve efficiency, quality, and scalability
* Ensure engineering and process solutions comply with USDA, FDA, food safety, sanitary design, and regulatory requirements

Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence

* Build and lead a multi-site continuous improvement program, maintaining a prioritized project portfolio with defined savings targets validated with Finance
* Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving methodologies (such as A3, DMAIC, value stream mapping, changeover reduction, and standard work)
* Drive waste reduction, productivity improvement, and labor optimization initiatives
* Evaluate operational KPIs, including OEE, yield, labor productivity, and discards, and use data analytics to prioritize improvement opportunities
* Coach kitchen and production leaders and engineers in structured problem solving, and ensure improvements are standardized and sustained
* Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across operations

Kitchen & Production Engineering

* Lead engineering efforts supporting highly automated meal production operations
* Drive equipment performance, uptime, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) improvements
* Identify ideal equipment required to produce Mom's Meals to specification at scale, including equipment that should be replaced or decommissioned and equipment that can deliver OEE improvements and a measurable return on investment
* Partner with Production leadership and Commercialization team to identify bottlenecks and improve throughput
* Lead facility expansion projects, line installations, equipment upgrades, and process redesign initiatives

Capital & Automation Projects

* Develop and manage the engineering capital plan, prioritizing projects by safety, quality, and measurable return
* Lead project prioritization, design, budgeting, vendor selection, implementation, and startup activities
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, and within budget
* Manage external engineering firms, contractors, equipment suppliers, and system integrators
* Build a practical, multi-year automation roadmap focused on productivity, yield, and labor efficiency
* Establish project governance, reporting, and post-implementation performance reviews

Maintenance & Reliability Partnership

* Partner with Maintenance leadership on standards for asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and preventative, predictive, and reliability-centered maintenance practices
* Use maintenance KPIs, including downtime, PM completion rates, equipment failure rates, and maintenance costs, to prioritize engineering and improvement work

Leadership & Team Development

* Provide coaching, mentorship, and technical leadership to process engineering, continuous improvement, and engineering personnel
* Develop future engineering leaders, improvement practitioners, and technical subject matter experts
* Promote a culture focused on safety, engagement, accountability, and operational excellence

### **Required Skills and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field
* 10+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience within manufacturing, food production, and highly automated operations, including leading process engineering or continuous improvement teams
* Hands-on experience applying Lean and Six Sigma tools, with a demonstrated record of delivering quantified, sustained savings and performance gains
* Strong process engineering skills, including process design, root cause analysis, process capability, statistical analysis, and OEE and yield analytics
* Demonstrated success leading capital projects and automation implementations, including equipment installations and line upgrades
* Working knowledge of industrial automation, controls, packaging systems, and manufacturing technologies
* Knowledge of Sanitary Design Principles and Standards for food manufacturing.
* Experience leading teams in regulated manufacturing environments
* Proven ability to influence cross-functional leaders and drive enterprise-wide change

### **Preferred Skills and Experience**

* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification
* Food manufacturing, packaged goods, pharmaceutical, and automated distribution experience
* Experience with Industry 4.0 technologies, predictive maintenance, and digital manufacturing tools
* Experience managing and understanding facility utility controls, including HVAC, water, and steam systems
* Professional Engineer (PE) license or advanced technical degree

**Company Overview**

Mom’s Meals is a home-delivered meal service providing fully prepared, refrigerated meal solutions direct to homes nationwide since 1999. We provide seniors, patients recovering post-discharge and those managing a chronic condition with tailored nutrition solutions to manage their specific needs. If you are passionate about the well-being of others and have a strong sense of community, Mom’s Meals could be the place for you! We are a family operated business looking for fun, compassionate, and friendly people who want to make a difference in the lives of others.

 

**EEO**

Mom’s Meals complies with all applicable federal and state non-discrimination laws. Qualified applicants shall receive consideration for employment without regards to race, religion, national origin, ancestry, color, gender, age, disability, or veteran status.
