The **Director of Quality & Compliance** is responsible for leading LOPA’s overall quality strategy, overseeing the agency’s Quality Management System (QMS) and ensuring that all products, services, and internal processes meet or exceed internal and external customer expectations and regulatory standards. Reporting to the Chief Strategy Officer, the position partners with operational leaders to translate requirements and quality findings into effective, measurable practices, fostering an agency-wide culture of integrity and operational excellence.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Quality Strategy & QMS Governance**

* **Quality Management System.** Own, maintain, and continuously improve the agency-wide QMS aligning objectives with organizational priorities and applicable standards.
* **Program Implementation**. Lead implementation and standardization of quality initiatives, establish milestones and accountabilities, monitor adoption, and assess ongoing effectiveness and sustainability.
* **Policies.** Oversee agency-wide development, implementation, including version control, approval workflows for all controlled documents. Support operational owners on content development and enforcement of policies and procedures.

**Regulatory Compliance & Audits**

* **Compliance Oversight.** Monitor compliance with applicable CMS requirements, OPTN policies and FDA regulations and other relevant industry standards and local and federal government regulations.
* **Audit Readiness and Management.** Oversee internal quality audits of donation and business processes to ensure regulatory and policy compliance, leveraging operational data to advise internal stakeholders on corrective actions; ensure ongoing monitoring of implemented changes to assess long-term effectiveness and sustainability. Serve as the primary liaison during external regulatory inspections and customer audits. Oversee agency’s response to any findings or observations from external audit.
* **Quality records.** Ensure quality records and compliance documentation are accurate, controlled, retrievable and inspection ready.

**Continuous Improvement & CAPA**

* **Root-Cause Analysis.** Oversees LOPA’s Occurrence Management Program to investigate instances of procedural non-conformance, resolve systemic issues, and prevent recurrence.
* **Data and KPIs.** Establish quality metrics, track key performance indicators (KPIs), and analyze statistical trends to identify efficiency gains within the QMS.
* **Support Process Optimization.** Partner with Operations leadership and the Performance Excellence team to embed quality and drive excellence in all process improvement initiatives.

**Leadership & Supplier Management**

* **Team Development.** Recruit, coach develop and evaluate a team of auditors and quality team members by setting priorities and performance expectations.
* **Supplier Quality.** Oversee vendor qualification, auditing, and performance monitoring to ensure specifications are met.
* **Customer Relations.** Collaborate directly with customers to resolve quality complaints, review technical specifications, and improve satisfaction.
* **Escalation:** Promptly communicates significant quality or regulatory concerns to CSO and recommend protective or corrective measures.

Requirements:

**Degree.** Bachelor’s degree in Quality Management, Life Sciences, Public Health, Business, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.

**Experience.** Minimum of five (5) years of progressive experience in quality management, assurance and/or control, regulatory compliance, auditing or related functions within a highly regulated environment, including at least two (2) years of supervisor, management or demonstrated functional leadership experience.

**Implementation Experience.** Demonstrated experience implementing, managing or enhancing quality management systems, regulatory compliance programs, or organization quality initiatives required.

**Industry Background.** Proven track record of applying knowledge of the principles of quality assurance/quality control. Experience within healthcare or donation and transplantation preferred.

**Skills & Certifications.** Certified Quality Manager (ASQ CMQ/OE), Six Sigma Black Belt, or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) strongly preferred.

**Technical Expertise.** Deep working knowledge of senior leadership of a Quality System. Experience applying CMS, OPTN, and FDA standards and regulations preferred.

**Leadership.** Exceptional cross-functional communication, strong decision making and problem-solving capabilities; analytical thinker with keen ability to resolve conflict and influence executive stakeholders, adept at managing agency-wide change.

**A Brief Overview**

The Director of Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for clinical quality, patient safety, regulatory readiness, accreditation compliance, and organizational policy management across a large, complex medical center. The Director establishes priorities, ensures alignment across clinical and operational functions, and partners with physician, nursing, operational, and administrative executives to advance high reliability, continuous improvement, regulatory excellence, and patient-centered care. This position has accountability for the design, execution, and sustained performance of quality improvement, patient safety, accreditation, policy governance, performance measurement, and regulatory compliance programs. The Director translates organizational strategy into medical center-wide priorities, evaluates performance and risk, directs corrective action, and provides executive leaders with recommendations needed to achieve organizational goals and external standards.

**What You Will Do**

* **Quality and Performance Improvement**
  + Establish and lead the organization's quality, safety, accreditation, and policy strategy in alignment with organizational strategy and medical center priorities.
  + Set the performance improvement agenda and direct organization-wide and departmental initiatives, including prioritization, resource allocation, accountability, and sustainability of results.
  + Establish performance expectations and governance for key quality indicators, publicly reported measures, regulatory metrics, and improvement commitments; intervene when performance or compliance is at risk.
  + Facilitate data-driven improvement efforts using Lean, Six Sigma, PDSA, and other improvement methodologies.
  + Own the integrity, interpretation, and executive communication of quality dashboards, scorecards, and performance reporting, including recommendations for action and escalation.
  + Partner with physician and nursing leaders to improve clinical outcomes, reliability, equity, and patient experience.

existing_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.**  
  
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

The role offers the opportunity to influence the quality standard for a growing federal business and help prepare the organization to support additional federal programs over time.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

  

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

  

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) facility and meaningful pharmaceutical distribution, logistics or 3PL quality exposure.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

  

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.
Direct leadership of quality teams  

  
  

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

  

* Remote work environment with regular computer and video-conference use.
* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.
* Ability to move through operating areas and wear required personal protective equipment when visiting sites.
* Flexibility to support audits, client needs or quality events outside standard business hours when required.

Eligibility Requirement: This position is open only to U.S. citizens due to applicable federal requirements. By applying, you confirm that you are a U.S. citizen and can provide acceptable documentation verifying your status if selected.  
  
If you are not a U.S. citizen, please do not apply for this role.

Cart.com is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

**Job Description Summary**

The Site Quality Director is responsible for ensuring cGMP compliance and product quality at the Raleigh, NC facility while supporting broader site quality initiatives aligned with company objectives. This role provides strategic leadership in the development, implementation, and oversight of the site quality systems to ensure that all manufacturing, testing, packaging, storage, and distribution activities meet regulatory standards and deliver the highest product quality. The Site Quality Director leads and mentors quality teams, oversees daily quality operations, and serves as a key partner to site leadership by providing guidance on quality and compliance across the organization.

**Job Description**

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* **Manages all aspects of Site Quality System including but not limited to: CAPA, exceptions, document management, complaint investigation handling, change control, supplier quality, OOS investigations, stability programs, and regulatory inspection readiness.**
* **Support a quality program which instils personal accountability for accuracy, consistency, and completeness for all operations**

* **CAPA program to effectively identify and correct problems that impact product quality or compliance.**

Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by *TIME* as a “Best Invention”, *MIT Technology Review* as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and *Fast Company* as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**

**Role Description**
--------------------

Form Energy is looking for an experienced Senior Director of Quality to join our battery manufacturing organization. In this role you will lead the Quality department for Form Energy. Your scope will be company-wide and your team will implement systems and processes that ensure products are designed, manufactured and shipped to the highest levels of performance, reliability, and quality.

This role is for an executive leader with experience developing new technologies and bringing high-volume manufacturing facilities to life. You will provide vision, strategy and leadership to help Form achieve manufacturing scale, cost-reduction, and daily operation execution.

As the key driver for shipping the highest quality products, you will thrive when working closely with leadership and cross-functional teams throughout the product development lifecycle, from early R&D to validation testing, pilot builds, and ultimately commercial production of customer-facing products.

*Relocation assistance is available.*

### **What you'll do:**

* Develop and sustain a world-class quality management system powered by a highly-trained, flexible, and proactive staff
* Maintain product risk profiles and manage quality systems to ensure Form Energy is meeting or exceeding risk expectations
* Ensure Form Energy production operations are releasing only conforming products to our customers
* Communicate key risks and opportunities to leadership and provide direction to resolve top issues and drive definitive corrective action
* Plan and efficiently manage Quality resources (labor, OpEx, and CapEx) and report on department performance and needs
* Communicate Form Energy's commitment to quality with internal and external interested parties
* Drive a customer-focused culture anchored by strong individual ownership and accountability

### **What you'll bring:**

* At least 10 years experience in quality, manufacturing, or manufacturing engineering
* At least 5 years in a senior-leader / site-leader quality role, demonstrating a clear record of success in building industry-leading teams that can execute in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
* Expertise in building Quality Management Systems (e.g., IATF 16949, ISO9001).
* Highly technical background, with a strong foundation in logical reasoning that allows for a steep learning curve and the ability to adapt to new technologies
* Excellent leadership, project management, communication, and organizational skills
* Bachelor’s Degree (or higher) in Engineering

### **Where you'll work:**

**As the VP, Quality Assurance & Food Safety**, you’ll report to the Bakery President and lead food safety, quality assurance, sanitation, and technical services across two bakery plants totaling more than 160,000 square feet and supporting more than 600 staff members. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact: setting the strategy, rebuilding organizational trust, strengthening audit readiness, and elevating Good Manufacturing Practices through disciplined root cause analysis and corrective action. You’ll operate at both the executive and plant levels, bringing the leadership, technical expertise, and influence needed to create lasting change.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **A Trusted Executive Leader:** You build credibility through transparency, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through, earning the confidence to influence decisions at every level.
* **A Strategic, Hands-On Quality Leader:** You set the vision while staying connected to operations, understanding risk, removing barriers, and translating strategy into consistent execution.
* **An Audit and Compliance Expert:** You build a culture of year-round readiness where issues are identified early, corrective actions are effective, and findings are sustainably closed.
* **A Disciplined Problem Solver:** You look beyond the immediate issue, using data, risk assessment, and root cause analysis to solve systemic problems and prevent recurrence.

**Responsibilities**

* Set and lead the Bakery division’s Quality Assurance and Food Safety strategy across both facilities, establishing clear expectations for risk management, performance, and accountability.

The answer is clear: your next opportunity starts here. Transform the future with us.

For more information about Modexus Solutions, visit www.modexussolutions.com

**Position Description**
------------------------

This role represents a critical executive leadership opportunity for a dynamic Director of Operations – Chillers to join the Global Operations team. Reporting directly to the VP of Global Operations with a dotted-line relationship to the Vice President & General Manager (VPGM) of the Chillers business unit, this leader has direct operational responsibility for all global chiller manufacturing plants.

Each global chiller facility holds full SQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) execution accountability. To drive self-sufficient, world-class execution at the plant level, the Director of Operations – Chillers will lead a comprehensive, multi-functional organization where each plant team includes dedicated Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations resources.

As an integral member of the Global Operations team, this individual operates as an influential peer to Supply Chain (partnering to enable global Supply Chain and SIOP execution) and Materials (partnering to enable Materials management and Localized Procurement strategies), as well as the broader Global Operations leadership team. By bridging global functional capabilities with plant-level execution and business unit strategy, the Director of Operations – Chillers will drive rapid operational transformation, capacity expansion, and sustainable business growth.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **1. Global Plant Leadership & SQDC Execution Accountability**

* Hold direct operational oversight and P&L/conversion cost accountability for all global chiller manufacturing facilities.
* Drive rigorousSQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) daily management and execution across every chiller site:

* **Safety:** Champion a zero-injury culture, ensuring proactive EHS compliance, ergonomic improvements, and behavioral safety leadership across all plants.
* **Quality:** Ensure zero-defect manufacturing standards, robust quality management systems, customer compliance, and rapid root-cause corrective actions.
* **Delivery:** Achieve industry-leading on-time delivery (OTD) and lead-time competitiveness through effective line balancing, capacity tracking, and constraint management.
* **Cost:** Optimize direct and indirect labor productivity, overhead absorption, scrap reduction, and continuous conversion cost improvements.

### **2. Multi-Functional Team Management & Talent Development**

* Lead, mentor, and develop Plant Managers and site leadership teams across the global chiller footprint.

**Job Responsibilities Continued**

* **Business Unit Alignment (Dotted Line to VPGM of Chillers):** Serve as a strategic operational partner to the VPGM of Chillers, translating commercial growth strategies, customer requirements, and new product introductions (NPI) into scalable manufacturing execution plans.

* **Global Operations Synergy:** Collaborate with fellow peers on the Global Operations leadership team to standardize best practices, leverage shared subassembly/hub strategies, and drive enterprise-wide operational initiatives.

### **4. Operational Excellence, Footprint Strategy & Continuous Improvement**

* Define and execute the end-to-end global manufacturing strategy for the Chillers business, aligning footprint optimization, capital investments (CapEx), and automation roadmaps with long-term growth targets.
* Embed Lean manufacturing principles, 80/20 simplification, value-stream mapping, and continuous improvement methodologies across all global chiller sites.

**Required Education & Qualifications**
---------------------------------------

* **Bachelor’s degree** in Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related technical discipline is required.

**DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS**

*Ritchey Livestock ID* | Fort Collins, Colorado | Full-Time, Onsite

Run the Operation. Build the Team. Shape What's Next.

**This Role Is For Builders.**

**We're looking for someone who can run a great operation today—and help build the company we'll become tomorrow.**

At Ritchey Livestock ID, we believe farmers and ranchers are the unsung heroes of our world. They work long hours, in every kind of weather, doing the essential work of feeding the rest of us. They don't ask for much in return. The least we can do is get our little part right.

For more than 60 years, we've manufactured livestock identification tags that ranchers can count on. Our products may be small, but the responsibility we feel to our customers is anything but.

We're a profitable, growing American manufacturer with a loyal nationwide customer base. We've recently completed the largest facility investment in our company's history, opening a new manufacturing operation in Fort Collins, Colorado. Now we're building the people, systems, and culture to carry Ritchey into its next chapter.

**We're looking for a hands-on Director of Operations who can lead that effort—and potentially grow into a broader executive leadership role as the company evolves.**

This is not a position for someone who wants to lead from behind a desk. You'll spend meaningful time on the production floor, working alongside your managers, solving real problems, and helping people succeed.

You'll also be expected to think beyond today's production schedule: developing leaders, building systems, improving performance, and preparing Ritchey for its next stage of growth.

**The Opportunity**

You'll lead approximately 45 people across manufacturing, engraving, shipping, and related operations, working directly with our CEO.

Your mission is twofold: **Run an exceptional operation today. Build the people, processes, and accountability that make excellence repeatable tomorrow.**

You'll own performance across safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, cost, and team development.

You'll be responsible for developing department managers, improving operational systems, driving continuous improvement, and building a culture where people take pride in their work and ownership of their results.

**Your First Year: Real Challenges, Real Opportunity**

We've made a major investment in our future. Now comes the work of making that investment pay off.

Here are five challenges you'll help us tackle:

* **Strengthen our new manufacturing operation.** Continue ramping up our Fort Collins facility, improving production stability, quality, capacity, and efficiency.
* **Improve scheduling and throughput.** Build better production planning and workflows across manufacturing, engraving, and shipping to improve delivery performance and reduce bottlenecks.
* **Build systems that last.** Reduce dependence on individual employees by developing practical SOPs, standardized processes, clear performance measures, and repeatable operating routines.
* **Develop our next generation of leaders.** Coach newer managers, strengthen accountability, and build employee development practices that help great people grow.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Use Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and practical root-cause problem-solving to reduce waste, improve productivity, and create measurable, sustainable improvements.

You'll have meaningful ownership of these challenges, the support of our leadership team, and the freedom to make a lasting impact.

**Who We're Looking For**

We're looking for a rare combination of heart, head, and hands. Someone who can lead people, build systems, solve problems, and roll up their sleeves when the work demands it.

**What you must bring:**

* **Proven People Leadership:** Demonstrated success leading teams in a manufacturing or production environment, ideally 20 or more employees, with experience developing supervisors or managers and holding people accountable.
* **Demonstrated Systems Building:** A track record of improving processes, implementing operational improvements, and building systems that continue to work without your constant involvement.
* **High Agency & Ownership:** The judgment, initiative, work ethic, and follow-through to take responsibility for results, solve difficult problems, and lead confidently in a hands-on environment.

**What we'd love to see:**

* Experience in plastic injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing processes.
* Practical experience applying Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement methods. Certifications are valued but not required.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, inventory management, purchasing, and quality systems.
* Strong financial and analytical skills, with an understanding of how operational decisions affect profitability.
* Experience developing managers, building teams, and helping an organization prepare for growth.

We value experience, but we're far more interested in what you've accomplished than the number of years on your résumé.

**Seasoned plastics professionals and exceptional leaders from other manufacturing environments are equally encouraged to apply.** What matters most is demonstrated leadership, systems thinking, operational judgment, and a willingness to keep learning.

***The Ritchey Way***

Our culture is built around one simple commitment: **DO RIGHT BY THE RANCH.**

Four core principles guide how we show up every day:

**ASK WHY. ASK WHAT IF.** — Learn the work. Make it better.

**MAKE THE SMALL THINGS COUNT.** — Bring care to the details, seen or unseen.

**NO SIDELINES.** — See it. Say it. Help solve it.

**BE GOOD TO WORK WITH.** — Carry your share. Be good company.

These aren't just words on a wall. They're the standards we hold ourselves and each other to. As our Director of Operations, you'll help bring *The Ritchey Way* to life through your leadership, your example, and the team you build.

**Why Ritchey?**

We're small enough that your ideas matter, but established and ambitious enough that your work can make a lasting difference. You'll have direct access to ownership, real authority to drive improvement, and a genuine opportunity to help shape the company's future.

**We're intentionally looking for someone with the potential to grow beyond operations.**

For the right individual who demonstrates exceptional leadership, business judgment, and results, this role could become a pathway toward broader company leadership, potentially including a future President or General Manager position.

That opportunity isn't guaranteed or tied to a timetable. It will be earned through performance, trust, and demonstrated ability to lead an increasingly complex business.

Most importantly, you'll be part of a team that takes pride in showing up every day for the farmers and ranchers who feed us.

**If you're a builder at heart, believe great people deserve great leadership, and want to create something you can be genuinely proud of, we'd love to meet you.**

**Location:** Fort Collins, Colorado — Full-Time, Onsite

**Compensation:** $130,000–$160,000 base salary, depending on experience and qualifications, plus performance-based bonus..

Pay: $130,000.00 - $160,000.00 per year

* Open & Honest - as a small company, we do not currently offer health benefits or a 401k. Our plan is to start to work on these things in 2027, but we prefer to meet you where we are today. Is that acceptable?
* How many years of practical experience do you have with concepts such as six sigma and lean manufacturing?

Animal health is key to the health of the planet. Working at Virbac means taking part in a unique human adventure in which the engagement of each individual contributes to its evolution. Finally, fostering their engagement to animal health also means listening to them and helping them to acquire new skills, preparing them for the challenges of tomorrow and encouraging them to contribute to an ever more responsible approach to our business.

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

Virbac Animal Health is seeking a Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology to join our Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) team. The Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology develops, implements, maintains, and improves robust manufacturing processes and facility infrastructure for right-first-time manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs. To plan, schedule, organize, and manage Technology Transfer Projects, CAPEX Engineering Projects, Validation, Technical Support, Alternate Raw Materials, Packaging, Life Cycle Management, and Team Leadership.

* Strong expertise in managing capital and operational expense budgets.
* Proven Leadership in process improvement , life cycle management, and technology transfers.
* In-depth knowledge of cGMP, EHS regulations, and sustainable engineering practices.

**Benefits:** 13 Company paid Holidays; 5 Floating Holidays (prorated); 15 vacation days (prorated); 5 floating holidays (prorated); 6% 401k match; competitive pay and bonus opportunity; growth opportunities within the department and much more!

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

**Area of responsibility 1: Technology Transfer Activities**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the budget, planning, and robust manufacturing (RFT for the first commercial batches) of technology transfer projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.

**Expected Results:** Successful, on-time, and on-budget delivery of facility, process, and product CAPEX engineering projects that enhance regional capacity, EHS standards, compliance, and efficiency.

**Area of responsibility 3:** Process Improvement & Life Cycle Management (LCM)

**Main Activities:**

**This is the future of modern energy. This is Celsius.**

Ready to take your career to the next level? Join our team and redefine what it means to be energized.

**Position Overview**
---------------------

As the Director of Manufacturing, you will serve as the senior plant leader for a high-volume beverage canning operation responsible for batching, filling, seaming, and packaging canned CELSIUS® beverages. You will provide strategic and operational leadership across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, safety, warehousing, workforce development, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who has operated in a high-speed, automated food, beverage, packaging, or consumer products environment. This role requires strong business judgment, operational discipline, technical understanding, and the ability to build an accountable, collaborative culture focused on safety, food safety, quality, service, cost, and continuous improvement.

**On-Site:** Based full-time in Charlotte, NC at Big Beverages manufacturing facility

**Travel Requirements:** Up to 25% domestic travel

**Reports To:** VP of Manufacturing

 **Requirements**  

* **Experience:** 7-10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, preferably in high-speed beverage filling/canning, food, or consumer packaged goods operations, including at least 3–5 years leading a plant or multi-department operation with full responsibility for production performance and hourly teams.
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Food Science, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
* Experience leading high-volume, automated manufacturing operations and managing production, maintenance, engineering, quality, safety, and continuous improvement functions.
* Working knowledge of FSSC 22000, ISO 22000 principles, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, food defense, food fraud prevention, traceability, prerequisite programs, CAPA systems, and audit readiness.
* Demonstrated success improving OEE, schedule attainment, throughput, labor efficiency, yield, waste, downtime, quality, cost performance, and equipment reliability through disciplined operating systems.
* Experience managing budgets, labor planning, capital projects, business cases, and plant-level financial performance.
* Experience hiring, developing, coaching, and leading large hourly and salaried teams, including supervisors and frontline leaders.
* Experience using ERP/MRP, MES, maintenance-management, and manufacturing-performance systems to make data-driven decisions.
* Strong analytical, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to work onsite at the manufacturing facility and support a flexible schedule based on operational needs.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* PCQI, HACCP, FSSC 22000, Lean Six Sigma, or similar certification or training.

* Experience with plant start-ups, expansions, new line installations, automation, commissioning, scale-up, or major capital investments.
* Experience supporting a rapidly growing consumer brand or publicly traded company.
* Experience working with labor relations or represented manufacturing environments.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all manufacturing operations to ensure the safe, efficient, and consistent production of high-quality canned beverages from production scheduling through finished-goods handoff.
* Develop and execute the plant operating strategy in alignment with CELSIUS business objectives, demand forecasts, customer requirements, and long-term growth plans.

* Ensure effective prerequisite programs, food defense, food fraud prevention, sanitation, traceability, lot control, allergen control where applicable, and environmental monitoring activities.
* Oversee inspections, testing, product release, holds, deviations, nonconforming product, complaints, CAPAs, and corrective-action effectiveness in partnership with Quality.
* Ensure beverage-specific quality controls are effective, including ingredient and batch accuracy, Brix and carbonation targets, fill levels and net contents, double-seam inspection, date/lot coding, and finished-product testing.
* Lead audit readiness and support certification, surveillance, recertification, customer, regulatory, internal, and third-party audits.
* Maintain a strong safety culture through employee engagement, training, audits, risk assessments, safety observations, incident investigations, emergency preparedness, and corrective-action plans.
* Collaborate with Human Resources to recruit, develop, retain, and engage a high-performing plant workforce.
* Build leadership capability through coaching, performance management, individual development plans, skills matrices, cross-training, succession planning, and consistent leader standard work.
* Lead labor planning and workforce optimization in response to production volumes, seasonality, new product requirements, and business growth.
* Manage the plant operating budget, labor costs, maintenance spending, capital expenditures, and other controllable expenses.
* Analyze operational and financial data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and actions needed to improve plant performance.
* Communicate plant performance, operating priorities, business risks, resource needs, and improvement plans clearly to plant and executive leadership.

* Leadership Expectations

The Director leads the Process Engineering Manager and the HVM Operations organization, integrating engineering priorities, manufacturing performance, and organizational capability. The role manages engineering and operations expenditure and execution in support of company objectives, and reports to the VP of Engineering.

**Primary Responsibilities:**

**Technical and Strategic Leadership**

* Set direction for process engineering and manufacturing operations, aligning objectives and priorities with company objectives cascaded by VP of Engineering, in partnership with senior management and JSR stakeholders.

* Align engineering and manufacturing to support long-term growth, capacity expansion, and product roadmap needs.
* Lead capital planning and manufacturing capacity expansion in partnership with Facilities, Equipment Engineering, and Maintenance, defining manufacturing requirements and coordinating execution of approved investments.

Develop plans and investment proposals to support VP in securing departmental budgets.

* Set priorities for the Process Engineering Manager, who leads the engineering team and owns process design, technical problem-solving, qualification, controlled process documentation, and technical readiness for transfer.
* Work with customer teams to balance production priorities against plant capacity, maintenance activities, equipment installs, and workforce readiness.
* Resolve significant technical, operational, customer-related, and cross-functional priority or resource conflicts within delegated authority; escalate decisions requiring additional approval to VP of Engineering.
* Lead organizational planning and develop the Process Engineering Manager, shift supervisors, and operations personnel to build leadership capability, technical depth, and operational continuity.

* Demonstrated experience managing engineering or manufacturing operating budgets and capital investment plans, including forecasting, resource allocation, cost management, and performance reporting.
* Demonstrated ability to connect technical priorities with safe, reliable manufacturing performance and make sound technical and operational trade-offs in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Experience:**

Lasko is seeking a Director of Plant Operations to lead our manufacturing facility in Franklin, Tennessee. This leader will oversee plant performance, with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee development.

The Director will translate business priorities into effective operating plans, strengthen manufacturing processes, and build a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. Working closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Human Resources, and Finance, this individual will ensure the facility consistently delivers quality products while improving productivity, controlling costs, and supporting Lasko's growth.

The ideal candidate is a visible, hands-on leader who builds strong teams, uses data to guide decisions, and maintains a consistent presence on the production floor.

**Key Responsibilities**

*Plant Leadership and Operational Performance*

* Lead daily plant operations, coordinating production, maintenance, manufacturing support, and material flow to meet safety, quality, cost, and delivery objectives.
* Develop and execute operating plans that align production capacity, staffing, equipment, and materials with business requirements.
* Establish clear performance expectations and operating metrics; review results regularly and drive corrective actions when performance falls short.
* Partner with Supply Chain and production planning teams to manage schedules, respond to changing demand, and maintain reliable customer service.
* Resolve operational challenges quickly while implementing lasting solutions that prevent recurring issues.

*Safety, Quality, and Compliance*

* Champion a culture in which employee safety is a daily priority and leaders take ownership of safe work practices.
* Oversee plant safety, environmental performance, and facility security in partnership with the appropriate support teams.
* Ensure consistent adherence to company policies, operating procedures, and applicable requirements.
* Partner with Quality and Engineering to improve process controls, reduce defects and rework, and ensure finished products meet established standards.
* Support audits, investigations, and corrective actions, ensuring timely follow-through and sustainable improvements

*Continuous Improvement and Manufacturing Excellence*

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives that increase throughput, improve equipment reliability, reduce waste, and strengthen overall plant performance.
* Apply Lean manufacturing principles, root cause analysis, standard work, and structured problem-solving to improve operating processes.
* Use production, quality, maintenance, and cost data to identify performance gaps and prioritize improvement opportunities.
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering to strengthen preventive maintenance programs and address equipment constraints.
* Support new product introductions, process changes, and manufacturing readiness to achieve successful production launches.

*Financial and Resource Management*

* Develop and manage plant operating budgets, monitor spending, and take action to address cost variances.
* Improve labor productivity, material utilization, energy efficiency, and material handling costs while maintaining safety and quality standards.
* Partner with Finance and Supply Chain to strengthen inventory accuracy, control work in process, and support effective inventory management.
* Identify and prioritize capital investment needs; develop business cases for equipment upgrades, automation, and facility improvements.
* Ensure people, equipment, and materials are deployed effectively to meet production commitments.

*People Leadership and Development*

* Build, coach, and develop a strong plant leadership team with clear responsibilities and measurable goals.
* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, hiring, onboarding, training, performance management, and employee relations.
* Foster a respectful, collaborative environment that encourages employee involvement, open communication, and ownership of results.
* Develop leadership capabilities and succession plans to support long-term operational stability.
* Maintain effective communication across shifts and departments to ensure consistent priorities and execution.

*Qualifications*

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including substantial leadership responsibility for plant performance and people management.
* Demonstrated success leading a manufacturing facility or a significant manufacturing operation with responsibility for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee development.
* Strong understanding of production planning, inventory control, equipment maintenance, quality systems, and manufacturing cost drivers.
* Experience developing and managing operating budgets, evaluating capital investments, and improving financial performance.
* Demonstrated ability to lead continuous improvement initiatives and deliver measurable operational results.
* Strong analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to balance immediate production needs and longer-term priorities.
* Effective communication skills and the ability to work across all levels of the organization.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and experience using ERP systems and manufacturing performance data.

*Preferred Qualifications*

* Experience in consumer products or another high-volume manufacturing environment.
* Familiarity with injection molding, assembly operations, automation, and related manufacturing processes.
* Experience leading operations across multiple shifts and managing seasonal changes in production demand.
* Lean or Six Sigma training or certification.
* Experience leading organizational change, developing plant leaders, and strengthening employee engagement.

*Work Environment*

This position is based onsite at Lasko's Franklin, TN manufacturing facility and requires regular presence on the production floor. Flexibility is required to support plant operations across shifts and address business needs.

**About Lasko Products**

**DEFINITION:**

Under general direction from the General Manager, plans, directs, organizes, integrates and provides oversight of ReGen Monterey’s Materials Recovery Facility (MRF), equipment maintenance, site and facilities maintenance, landfill operations; scales operations, landfill gas operations, and Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) operations; directs and manages the development of short and long-term goals and objectives consistent with the Strategic Plan and annual business plan and ensures their effective execution; ensures all assigned operations and functions serve the needs of ReGen Monterey, while complying with applicable laws and regulations; responsible for maximizing the environmental management of resources; provides highly responsible and complex operations support to the General Manager.

**DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:**

This position is responsible for coordination, integration and short and long-range planning of a wide variety of functions related to solid waste processing, recycling and diversion programs for ReGen Monterey. Incumbents work at an advanced professional level on complex and specialized solid waste-related operations, recycling activities, facilities, programs, and services, which include formulation and implementation of programs and financial budgets. Within assigned areas of accountability, the incumbent operates with substantial latitude and discretion to achieve effective and efficient utilization of resources in serving ReGen Monterey’s mission. Positions at this class level serve as a member of ReGen’s leadership team and provide advice and counsel to the General Manager regarding strategic policy and problem-solving issues relating to the assigned Departments and ReGen’s overall. A person appointed to the Director of Operations classification is an “at-will” employee.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

*The following duties are typical of this classification and are intended only to describe the various types of work that may be performed, the level of technical complexity of the assignment(s) and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of duties. The omission of a specific duty statement does not exclude it from the position if the work is consistent with the concept of the classification or is similar or closely related to another duty statement to address business needs and changing business practices.*

* Oversee and is responsible for planning and execution of all aspects of solid waste and recycling operations including processing, recycling/diversion, scheduling, expansion and renovation of processing facility, and customer service.
* Oversee logistics, material preparation and export compliance of collected materials and manage all aspects of commodity sales and related contracted services.
* Oversees and is responsible for the planning and execution of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of ReGen Monterey’s landfill; oversees proper compliance with specifications on the use and development of disposal site, ensures proper operations compliance with health and safety regulations.
* Participates in the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies, and priorities of ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Plans, organizes, controls, integrates and evaluates the work of assigned departments to ensure services comply with the policies and strategic direction set by the General Manager, Board of Directors and all applicable laws and regulations.
* Recommend and enforce State waste reduction/recycling regulations and other policy issues, including safety policy and procedures.
* Manages the development, revision, and implementation of policies and procedures for ReGen Monterey’s solid waste and recycling/diversion operations.
* Drafts budget for assigned departments.
* Reviews and assesses all program production data; measures program effectiveness; prepares quarterly and annual data reports.
* Assists in the preparation of Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for equipment and services; represents the division in negotiations with vendors and service contractors and participates in contract administration in disputed contractual matters.
* Prepares staff reports and letters, including reports for presentation to Board of Directors.
* All ReGen Monterey positions require the employee to provide good customer service to both internal and external customers, maintain positive and effective working relationships with other ReGen Monterey employees, and have regular and reliable attendance and timeliness. Must show cooperation and respect to fellow employees and supervisors at all times.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBLITIES:**

The incumbent in this position provides direct supervision of the operations department managers and has oversight of multiple departments and indirect supervision of approximately 100 assigned department employees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Through subordinates, supervises the safe and efficient handling and disposal of solid waste, including household, industrial, infectious, medical, and household hazardous materials; provides oversight ancillary solid waste operations, including equipment maintenance and repair, recycling, and enforcement of refuse disposal laws.
* Coordinates solid waste processing operations with engineering staff to ensure the success of new programs and facilities; analyzes field operations and formulates improvements to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations; performs long-range planning for staffing needs, equipment replacement, and other operational requirements.
* Provides oversight to HHW program and organics recycling program, including food waste collection, yard waste processing, mulch/compost marketing and other waste reduction processing such as scrap metal, electronic waste, mattresses, and scrap tires.

* Prepares tonnage reports and makes recommendations regarding change in fees.
* Organize and optimize the structure of the assigned departments, adjusting in accordance with workloads and new/changing functions.
* Maintain contact with various governmental and regulatory agencies, industry related agencies, and represent ReGen Monterey at public and professional organizations functions.
* Selects and trains operations staff; assists management staff in resolving the most difficult operational problems; establishes productive standards and measures staff performance; accordingly, prepares annual performance plans, evaluates performance, and reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinate managers. Collaborates with human resources with disciplinary actions.
* Directly or through subordinates, responds to complaints from ReGen Monterey customers by explaining and enforcing applicable laws and regulations; participates in public workshops to explain and generate support for proposed projects and facilities; may address the Board of Directors to answer questions about issues or proposals related to ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Oversees and participates in the annual review and revision of ReGen Monterey’s fee structure; develops strategies and approaches for evaluating fee change alternatives; directs the development and recommends proposed fees; attends and participates in public meetings; oversees the implementation of new fees following board approval.
* Directs and coordinates the preparation of analyses and recommendations regarding policy issues and long-range plans to address ReGen Monterey’s financial needs; advises the General Manager regarding policy issues, programs and projects to meet ReGen Monterey and customer needs; advises and assists the General Manager in identifying, articulating and implementing policies, programs and projects.
* Participates in the analysis of proposed legislation and regulation; participates in industry and intergovernmental activities to influence legislative and regulatory change consistent with ReGen Monterey’s interests and needs; represents ReGen Monterey as requested or assigned in dealings with stakeholders in ReGen Monterey’s service area, and with other industry and governmental agencies and professional organizations.
* Participates in major negotiations with contractors, consultants, vendors, collective bargaining and other public agencies.
* Participates in regional, state, national and other professional meetings and conferences to stay abreast of trends and technology related to ReGen Monterey’s operations, particularly in areas of assigned accountability.

**Knowledge of and Ability to:**

The following generally describes the knowledge and ability required to successfully perform the assigned duties.

**Knowledge of:**

Principles and practices of recycling and diversion program operations, solid waste management and landfill maintenance practices and procedures; local, state and federal regulations pertaining to environmental management of landfills and public works systems or landfill operations; California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); principles and practices of budgeting, effective management, supervision, evaluation and training; health and safety regulations. Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint) is required.

**Ability to:**

**TRAINING, EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in environmental planning and management; environmental studies; solid waste planning or a related field is required.

**Experience:**

* Ten to 15 years of broad and progressively responsible work experience in recycling program operations, transfer station management, or combined and related experiences.
* A minimum of five years of recent experience in solid waste management and/or in the operation of mixed waste processing facility or a single-stream material recovery facility or operation of a landfill is required. **OR** work experience in a management position with a private or public agency responsible for solid waste management, recycling/diversion or landfill operations to demonstrate knowledge, skills, and abilities to meet the above minimum requirements.

**License or Certificate:**

* Possession of a valid California driver’s license is required.

**Physical Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to sit; talk or hear, in person, in meetings and by telephone; use hands to finger, handle, feel or operate standard office equipment; and reach with hands and arms; occasionally bend, stoop, lift and/or carry objects weighing up to 25 pounds individually. Employees are occasionally required to walk and stand on even and uneven surfaces, grounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

**Mental Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to use written and oral communication skills; read and interpret complex data, information and documents; analyze and solve complex policy and operational problems; observe and interpret people and situations; use math and mathematical reasoning; learn and apply new information or skills; perform highly detailed work on multiple, concurrent tasks with constant interruptions; work under intensive deadlines and interact with Board members, all levels of ReGen Monterey management, other elected and appointed governmental officials, consultants, contractors, developers, vendors, employees, media representatives and the public.

**Special Demands**

Must be able to actively participate in public meetings, including giving presentations in person and on camera before the Board of Directors and members of the public.

Employees work under typical office conditions, and the noise level is usually quiet, occasional exposure to dirt, grease, foul odors and other outdoor elements.

Our colleague experience is an area of obsessive focus. At DeVry University, we care about you. Because, only through you can we deliver our unique Care Formula to our learners and partners.
  
  
Opportunity
  
The Program Director, Advanced Manufacturing Technology, will lead the development and launch of employer-informed technical education programs in advanced manufacturing. Working across Product and Academics, this role translates industry requirements into differentiated academic programs, identifies delivery and investment needs, and coordinates academic and product readiness for launch.
  
The position provides discipline-level leadership and accountability for the Advanced Manufacturing Technology program from initial development through sustainable academic operations. During program build and launch, the role will operate within Product in close partnership with Academics. Once the program is established, the position may transition to Academics and assume ongoing leadership of a faculty team, instructional quality, academic operations, and program performance, consistent with institutional academic governance and approval requirements.
  
Responsibilities
  
Employer Engagement and Program Strategy
  

* Establish and maintain a structured process for engaging employers and industry stakeholders to identify required competencies, knowledge, skills, abilities, and employment outcomes.
* Develop relationships with employers and industry partners that could support program co-design, applied learning opportunities, industry-recognized credentials, or pathways to employment.
* Use employer feedback, labor-market demand, competitive intelligence, and recognized industry competency frameworks to inform program direction and differentiation.

Program and Curriculum Development

* Identify opportunities to differentiate DeVry’s programs through emerging technologies, simulation, industry partnerships, innovative hands-on learning models, and integration of digital technologies.

* Coordinate input from faculty, academic leaders, and industry partners to maintain program relevance and quality.

Investment and Delivery Planning
  

* Develop recommendations and funding requirements for labs, equipment, tools, technology, facilities, instructional resources, and external delivery partnerships.
* Evaluate delivery options that expand learner access, support hands-on skill development, improve the student experience, and create efficient, scalable operations.
* Partner with Finance and operational teams to evaluate program costs, investments, and implementation requirements.

Program Operations, Resource Stewardship, and Performance
  

* Provide accountable discipline-level leadership for operational readiness and sustained delivery, including instructional scheduling coordination, lab and equipment utilization, safety-related instructional requirements, and issue resolution with relevant operational partners.
* Develop and monitor program-level operating plans, resource needs, and budget recommendations; partner with Finance and academic leadership to manage approved resources, evaluate cost-to-deliver, and identify opportunities for quality, access, and operational efficiency.
* Demonstrate the ability to lead faculty or technical instructional teams, manage academic delivery, and drive measurable program quality and student outcomes.
* Apply experience with program-level resource planning, budget stewardship, operational improvement, and coordination of facilities or lab-based instruction.
* Own discipline-specific performance improvement recommendations and execution within delegated authority, escalating material investment, regulatory, or strategic decisions to appropriate institutional leaders.
* Lead the transition from product launch to academic operations, including documented handoffs, faculty management readiness, operating procedures, performance measures, and continuity of employer relationships.

Launch and Cross-Functional Execution
  

* Lead the discipline-specific academic and product workstreams of the go-to-market project, coordinating with Academics, Product, Regulatory Affairs, Marketing, Enrollment, Finance, and other teams.
* Monitor program design, approval, readiness, and launch milestones; identify dependencies, risks, and decisions requiring leadership attention.
* Support launch readiness and early program review, using employer and learner feedback to recommend improvements to quality, relevance, and outcomes.

Discipline-Specific Responsibilities
  

* Apply knowledge of advanced manufacturing technologies, industrial operations, automation, and related technician competencies to program design and employer engagement.
* Evaluate relevant manufacturing competency frameworks, applied laboratory requirements, and industry-recognized credentials when developing program recommendations.

Academic Leadership and Faculty Management
  

* Following program establishment and transition to Academics, lead and manage assigned advanced manufacturing faculty, including hiring input, onboarding, performance evaluation, coaching, development, workload planning, and accountability for instructional effectiveness.

Qualifications
  

* Demonstrated experience in advanced manufacturing, industrial technology, automation, or a closely related technical field.
* Experience developing, launching, or substantially improving technical, career and technical education, or workforce-aligned academic programs.
* Ability to translate employer competency requirements into curriculum and practical learning experiences.
* Working knowledge of program approval processes, academic collaboration, and the operational requirements of hands-on technical education.
* Demonstrated ability to lead faculty or technical instructional teams, manage academic delivery, and drive measurable program quality and student outcomes.
* Experience with program-level resource planning, budget stewardship, operational improvement, and coordination of facilities or lab-based instruction.

* Demonstrates curiosity and adaptability in embracing emerging technologies, including AI, to improve work and outcomes. Uses these technologies thoughtfully, responsibly, and in alignment with organizational guidelines.

Preferred Qualifications
  

* Experience with manufacturing employers, industry associations, and recognized technical competency frameworks.
* Experience planning labs, equipment, faculty or instructor needs, and hybrid or technology-enabled technical instruction.

This position is eligible for an annual incentive bonus.

**Director, Facility Operations**  
The 3-time WNBA Champions Los Angeles Sparks are seeking an innovative, strategic, and revenue-driven **Director, Facility Operations**. This executive will be responsible for working with both in-house employees and 3rd party vendors, and will oversee the day-to-day upkeep and operation of the Los Angeles Sparks’ Training Facility.

**PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Oversee the operation of building systems and equipment, including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, hydro, and food service equipment and direct the work of personnel associated with the systems and building engineering.
* Serve at the primary point of contact for building maintenance, repairs, and facilities-related service requests across all organizational spaces, including offices and venues.
* Assist in the development and implementation of a computerized work order management system to enable occupants to submit service requests, track progress, and support the prioritization and scheduling of maintenance and repair activities.
* Serve as point of contact for local utilities (ex. Southern California Edison for building power).
* Serve as the primary building point of contact for the Fire Marshal, coordinate and attend required inspections, maintain all necessary fire and life safety records and documentation, and schedule and oversee required annual, quarterly, and other periodic testing of building safety systems in accordance with applicable codes and jurisdictional requirements.
* Build and maintain budgets for annual preventative maintenance costs.
* Develop and maintain appropriate inventory levels of supplies, materials, and repair parts based on facility and venue needs, ensuring materials are readily available to support maintenance and repair activities, and maintain accurate inventory records.
* Develop and oversee annual and preventive maintenance schedules for all facilities and building systems; establish and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) for facility operations, maintenance, and emergency response; and identify, engage, and manage third-party vendors to support venue operations, including establishing clear emergency response protocols and service expectation.
* Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, supply usage, labor, and associated costs to track facility performance, identify maintenance trends, and inform the development of a long-term asset management and replacement program Develop service contract requirements, scope of work, performance standards, and service-level expectations for third-party vendors to ensure facility maintenance and operational needs are clearly defined and consistently met.
* Oversee and direct housekeeping services and cleaning services for back of house spaces, player spaces, and office spaces.
* Demonstrate knowledge of professional sports hardwood court cleaning practices and maintenance requirements to ensure the playing surface meets the standards and operational needs of a professional sports team.
* Oversee and coordinate specialty window cleaning and other specialized cleaning services, ensuring work is performed safely, effectively, and in accordance with facility standards.
* Build and maintain strong working relationships with team personnel to understand facility-related needs and requests, coordinate service delivery, and ensure clear, timely, and consistent communication.
* Working alongside Food Service team and associated personnel, coordinate repairs to equipment essential to food and beverage operations as needed.
* Working alongside team trainers, schedule servicing hydrotherapy equipment as required.
* Oversee and direct the work of landscaping team to ensure trees and plants (indoor and outdoor) are maintained.
* Collect and maintain accurate records to track venue assets, with an ability to identify faulty equipment, or make recommendations based on anticipated lifecycle for asset replacement.
* Track warranties of building assets.
* Conduct frequent physical inspections of building and external grounds to ensure the highest industry standards are met in Maintenance, System Operations, identifying and communicating any potential safety concerns, and areas requiring follow-up attention.
* Other duties, as assigned, related to the upkeep, maintenance and operation of the Sparks’ Training Facility.

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in facility maintenance, building systems management, and facilities oversight, including supervisory or managerial responsibilities. Experience in a professional sports or large-scale venue environment is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge of building systems and facility maintenance, including HVAC systems (air- and water-cooled systems, humidity control, and ventilation), fire and life safety systems, electrical systems, plumbing, and exterior grounds maintenance. Ability to oversee preventive maintenance, troubleshoot facility issues, and coordinate specialized contractors to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient building operations.
* Experience leading maintenance personnel and managing third-party service providers, with the ability to establish maintenance standards, oversee service delivery, and ensure facilities meet the operational requirements of a professional sports organization.
* Understanding of basketball schedules and basic team operations.
* Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects simultaneously, working efficiently, to meet deadlines, with an excellent eye for detail.
* Strong interpersonal, organizational, computer and communication skills, as well as analytical skills.
* A proven ability to think critically and set priorities.
* Innovative thinker with success in developing and implementing new ideas and programs.
* Ability to anticipate and resolve problems and conflicts.
* Available to respond to emergencies 24/7.
* Ability to maintain a high level of Professionalism in all circumstances.
Ability to work frequent irregular and long hours, weekends, evenings and all full-stadium events through completion and departure of public and team personnel as appropriate.  

**Compensation commensurate with experience; minimum starting salary at $105,000 annually.**

The incumbent is expected to perform other duties necessary for the effective operation of the department and organization.
