existing_roles.title: Director, MSAT/External Manufacturing Management
existing_roles.description:
OPPORTUNITY

Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).

All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.

This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Process scale-up and technology transfer

* Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
* Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
* Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
* Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities

Process characterization and PPQ readiness

* Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
* Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
* Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification
* Partner with Analytical Development to make sure methods are phase-appropriate, validated on time and fit to support characterization and PPQ

External manufacturing and CDMO management

* Serve as Mammoth's technical lead and person-in-plant at CDMOs and contract labs for development, engineering and GMP campaigns
* Lead selection, qualification and oversight of CDMO partners for drug product manufacturing, fill-finish operations and drug product testing, including technical due diligence, capacity and capability assessment, and scale-up fit
* Provide technical oversight for engineering and GMP runs at external partners
* Develop scalable, phase-appropriate aseptic drug product processes at CDMOs, including fill-finish operations, cryogenic handling (as applicable) and cold-chain compatibility
* Assess and implement suitable container-closure systems (vials, syringes) that meet regulatory and operational requirements
* Accountable for review and approval of batch records in accordance with regulatory guidelines; review campaign plans, deviations, investigations, CAPAs and change controls in partnership with Quality
* Manage partner timelines, budgets, deliverables and quality in collaboration with internal stakeholders; drive technical decisions and escalate issues early
* Project manage external stakeholders and high-profile partner meetings (up to 10% of time)
* Contribute to technical sections of quality agreements, statements of work and budgets

Regulatory and cross-functional support

* Author and review CMC sections for IND/IMPD/CTA amendments, end-of-Phase 2 and later filings (Module 3 process description, process development history, process validation)
* Support regulatory interactions and inspections with process knowledge and data
* Provide manufacturing input to program plans, timelines and supply forecasts

Team and resource leadership

* In the early phase, deliver through external resources: CDMO technical teams, consultants and contract MSAT staff
* Build the internal MSAT function in stages tied to milestones, including hiring plans, roles and the balance of internal and outsourced work
* Set up MSAT systems and practices: tech transfer templates, process knowledge management, data trending and lifecycle documentation

### **REEQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* PhD in chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry or a related field with 10+ years of industry experience, or MS with 14+ or BS with 16+ years of experience
* 6+ years in MSAT, process development or technical operations for parenteral drug products, including at least 3 years in a leadership role
* Hands-on experience scaling up LNP or comparable complex parenteral processes (liposomes, nanoparticles, nucleic acid formulations) from early clinical to late-stage scale
* Led at least one process characterization and PPQ campaign through completion, with working command of ICH Q8–Q12 and FDA/EMA process validation expectations
* Extensive experience managing CDMOs and contract labs as the sponsor's technical lead, including tech transfer, person-in-plant oversight, deviations and change control
* Experience with fill-finish operations, aseptic processing and external manufacturing oversight
* Strong working knowledge of cryogenic storage and cold-chain management for LNP drug products
* Track record of authoring CMC regulatory sections and supporting agency interactions
* Ability to influence and direct external partners without line authority, and to make sound technical calls under timeline pressure
* Ability for frequent domestic and international travel to CDMO and contract lab sites, estimated at up to [30–40]% and peaking during engineering, characterization and PPQ campaigns
* Must be able to travel internationally on short notice and hold, or be able to obtain, a valid passport and any visas needed for partner sites
* Ability to commit to extended on-site presence at CDMOs (person-in-plant) during critical campaigns, sometimes across time zones.
* Based in the San Francisco Bay Area preferred, with ability to work onsite at our Brisbane, CA location; hybrid or remote arrangements are available
* Ability to work Pacific Time Zone hours if not located on the West Coast
* Ability to travel to Mammoth’s Brisbane, CA HQ regularly if not local

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Direct experience with mRNA/LNP or gene editing drug products
* Experience with impingement jet or microfluidic mixing scale-up, TFF and sterile filtration of LNPs
* Experience with commercial process validation and BLA/MAA preparation
* Experience building a function or team from the ground up in a small or mid-size biotech
* Working knowledge of statistical tools for DoE and process data analysis (e.g., JMP, Minitab)

### **BENEFITS**

* Company-paid health/vision/dental benefits
* Unlimited vacation and generous sick time
* Company-sponsored meals and snacks
* Wellness, caregiver and ergonomics benefits
* 401(k) with company matching

Actual base salary will be determined by relevant professional experience, applicable skills, and internal equity

**COMPANY**

Mammoth Biosciences is a biotechnology company focused on leveraging its proprietary ultracompact CRISPR systems to develop long-term curative therapies, as well as other applications such as decentralized precision diagnostics. Founded by CRISPR pioneer and Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Trevor Martin, Janice Chen, and Lucas Harrington, the company’s ultracompact proteins are designed to enable *in vivo* gene editing in difficult to reach tissues utilizing both nuclease applications and new editing modalities beyond double stranded breaks, including base editing, gene writing, and epigenetic editing. The company is building out its pipeline of potential *in vivo* gene editing therapeutics and capabilities and has partnerships with leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to broaden the reach of its innovative and proprietary technology. Mammoth’s deep science and industry experience, along with a robust and differentiated intellectual property portfolio, have enabled the company to further its mission to transform the lives of patients and deliver on the full promise of CRISPR technologies.

This policy covers all facets of employment including, but not limited to: recruitment, selection, placement, promotions, transfers, demotions, terminations, training, and compensation.

### **Description**

At Pacific Seafood, we do more than just provide the world with the healthiest proteins on the planet. We are a family-owned, excellence-driven organization committed to being the brand of choice in the marketplace and the employer of choice in the community. We believe in servant leadership, investing in our team members’ personal and professional growth, and rewarding performance. We live by the core values of our Diamond Philosophy: Teamwork, Productivity, Quality, and Excellence—which means consistently doing your best and *always* striving to do better.
  
  
**Summary:**

We are seeking a dynamic, solutions-oriented **Director of Technology Operations** to lead, scale, and optimize IT operations for our enterprise. Serving as a strategic partner to leadership and business unit heads across geographies, this role is accountable for the reliability, agility, and continuous evolution of our enterprise technology ecosystem.

The ideal candidate is a transformative, hands-on leader who blends deep technical fluency with strong financial stewardship and operational maturity. Rather than introducing rigid bureaucracy, this leader takes a pragmatic, evolutionary approach—fine-tuning existing workflows, aligning IT service delivery with measurable business outcomes, and fostering an empowering, "Best in Class" culture across Service Desk, Project Management Office (PMO), Infrastructure, and Enterprise Applications.

Because our team members are our greatest asset and strength, this role directly assesses the VP’s direct reports and the next level of leaders, identifies strengths and gaps, and ensures each leader has a practical development plan. The Director also evaluates reporting relationships, spans of control, role clarity, and succession depth, and uses a working knowledge of income statements and balance sheets to connect people decisions to business results.

### **Key Responsibilities**

**1. Enterprise IT Service Delivery & Service Desk Operations**

* **Support Leadership:** Direct the strategy and daily execution of end-user support, including the IT Service Desk, Desktop Support, Field Services, Depot/Procurement, and VIP/Executive Support across multiple time zones.
* **SLA & Throughput Excellence:** Establish, monitor, and enforce aggressive Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to ensure consistent, predictable service throughput—even during critical end-of-month, end-of-quarter, or high-volume operational periods.
* **End-to-End Lifecycle Management:** Oversee the complete IT lifecycle of internal and customer-facing systems, including enterprise workstations, telephony, infrastructure, and specialized operational/manufacturing hardware.
* **Operational Readiness & Business Continuity:** Lead contingency planning, risk surfacing, and operational readiness initiatives to protect business continuity and minimize disruptions during organizational transitions or major system cutovers.

**2. ITSM, ITIL Frameworks & IT Governance**

* **ITSM & ITIL Maturity:** Own, design, and continuously optimize core ITIL processes—including Incident, Problem, Request, Change, Escalation, and Knowledge Management—within enterprise platforms.
* **IT Intake & Demand Management:** Architect and govern a centralized IT Intake process to evaluate, prioritize, and route incoming business requests, ensuring resource allocation aligns with strategic corporate objectives and operational capacity.
* **Enterprise Governance & Compliance:** Establish pragmatic IT governance models, internal controls, and compliance frameworks that safeguard enterprise data and infrastructure without impeding business agility.
* **Knowledge & Self-Service Enablement:** Drive continuous improvement in knowledge base creation, documentation standards, and automated self-service tools to empower end-users and accelerate first-contact resolution.

**3. Project Management Office (PMO) & Digital Transformation**

* **PMO Leadership & Tollgate Governance:** Develop, deploy, and oversee formalized project management methodologies and tools. Serve as the executive tollgate for technology initiatives to ensure requirements are rigorously defined, scoped, and aligned with strategic goals.
* **Enterprise System Implementations:** Lead cross-functional execution for major digital transformation initiatives, including ERP migrations, CRM rollouts, and M&A technology integrations.
* **AI & Automation Readiness:** Champion the pragmatic adoption of emerging technologies and AI-driven workflows across IT operations to automate routine tasks, enhance reporting accuracy, and elevate enterprise productivity.

**4. Continuous Improvement & Lean Operations**

* **Lean Six Sigma Execution:** Embed Lean and Continuous Improvement methodologies into daily IT operations to eliminate waste, reduce turnaround times, and streamline cross-departmental workflows.
* **Root Cause & Corrective Action:** Partner closely with all IT Operations teams on deep failure-mode analysis and root-cause corrective actions to permanently resolve recurring technical issues and business impacts.
* **Asset & Inventory Optimization:** Reframe IT hardware, spare parts, and demo/recon pools as actively managed operational assets—optimizing space utilization, procurement costing, redistribution, and lifecycle disposition.

**5. Customer Satisfaction & Cross-Functional Partnership**

* **Customer-Centric Culture:** Champion an unwavering focus on internal and external customer satisfaction, transforming IT from a transactional support function into a proactive, trusted business enabler.
* **Executive & Departmental Alignment:** Foster transparent, collaborative partnerships with Finance, Manufacturing, Distribution, Quality, Engineering, and Sales leadership to ensure technology roadmaps directly support revenue and operational goals.
* **Voice of the Customer:** Implement regular satisfaction tracking, feedback loops, and executive business reviews to measure stakeholder sentiment and drive targeted service enhancements.

**6. Financial Stewardship & Resource Optimization**

* **Multi-Million-Dollar P&L Management:** Develop, justify, and manage a $15M–$30M+ IT operations budget, maintaining strict fiscal discipline across OPEX, CAPEX, vendor contracts, and software licensing.
* **Data-Driven Economics:** Apply rigorous cost-benefit and repair-versus-replace analyses to hardware maintenance, vendor agreements, and service models, identifying opportunities to reduce operational costs while improving service quality.
* **Vendor & Outsourced Partner Management:** Negotiate and manage contracts with third-party vendors, hardware suppliers, and managed service providers to ensure accountability and maximum return on investment.

**7. Talent Development & Organizational Leadership**

* **Inspirational People Leadership:** Lead, mentor, and coach a diverse, geographically dispersed organization of managers, engineers, analysts, and technicians.
* **Cross-Training & Team Resilience:** Eliminate single-point dependencies by building structured cross-training programs, clear career pathways, and flexible skill coverage across teams.
* **High-Accountability & Morale:** Cultivate a high-morale, low-turnover environment rooted in psychological safety, diversity, equity, and inclusion, while holding staff to clear performance standards through active coaching and accountability.

  

### **What you bring to Pacific Seafood**

**Required:**

* **Executive or Senior Leadership Track Record:** 12+ years of progressive leadership experience in IT Operations, Service Delivery, or Technical Operations, including 5+ years at the Director or Senior level within a complex, multi-site, or enterprise environment.
* **Proven Operational Impact:** Demonstrated history of scaling support teams, managing multi-million-dollar budgets, and delivering measurable reductions in operational costs and ticket turnaround times.
* **Enterprise Transformation:** Hands-on experience leading large-scale ERP/CRM transitions, ITIL/ITSM framework implementations, and post-M&A systems integration.
* **Cross-Industry Fluency:** Strong operational understanding of corporate IT alongside manufacturing, distribution, engineering, or field-service environments.

**Education & Certifications**

**Certifications, not required, but highly desired:**

* ITIL Certification

* Project Management Professional or active PMI affiliation strongly preferred.

**Physical Requirements**  
  
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the team member:

* Must be available to work Monday -Friday during regular working hours, with occasional weekend duties.

This role owns external manufacturing partnerships end to end, from partner selection, onboarding, and technology transfer through campaign execution and ongoing performance management, to ensure reliable, high-quality, and cost-effective manufacturing. The role also supports clinical supply needs by aligning external manufacturing output with clinical program timelines.

The role will partner closely with Technical Operations, Quality, CMC, Procurement, Clinical Operations, and senior leadership to drive strategic partner decisions, resolve risks, and build a scalable external manufacturing network. This is a high-visibility opportunity to shape the external manufacturing strategy of an innovative, growing cell therapy company.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Serve as the primary relationship owner for CMOs/CDMOs and critical suppliers, leading governance forums, joint steering committees, and executive-level engagement.
* Lead partner selection, due diligence, contracting support, and onboarding, including quality and supply agreements in partnership with Quality, Legal, and Procurement.
* Oversee technology transfers, process readiness, and manufacturing campaigns at external partners, driving timelines, deliverables, and issue resolution.
* Define and track partner performance metrics (delivery, quality, capacity, cost, and responsiveness); lead business reviews and improvement plans.
* Manage external manufacturing schedules, capacity planning, and batch-record and deliverable timelines across partners.
* Partner with Quality and Technical Operations on supplier qualification, audits, changes, deviations, CAPAs, and other GMP-related activities.
* Lead negotiation and management of commercial terms, pricing, change orders, and budgets in collaboration with Procurement and Finance.
* Proactively mitigate risks to partner capacity, critical materials, lead times, and supplier continuity; lead contingency and alternate-source strategies.
* Report on partner performance, risks, and mitigation plans to cross-functional stakeholders and senior leadership; mentor team members as the organization grows.
* Align external manufacturing output with clinical program timelines, working with the clinical supply team on forecasting, inventory planning, and IRT/RTSM needs.
* Support oversight of GMP packaging and manufacturing activities for clinical supply at external partners.
* Travel: Approximately 20–30% to CMO/CDMO and supplier sites, with flexibility based on program needs

**Qualifications**  
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Life Sciences, Engineering, Business, or related field; advanced degree a plus.
* 8+ years of experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, cell therapy, biologics, or another GMP-regulated environment, including significant CMO/CDMO and vendor management experience.
* Demonstrated success managing external manufacturing partners, including technology transfer, campaign execution, and performance management.
* Strong understanding of GMP requirements and biotech/pharmaceutical manufacturing and supply-chain processes.
* Strong leadership, relationship-management, negotiation, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and external partners.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, clinical-stage environment.

**Preferred**

* Cell therapy or advanced therapy experience.
* Experience with supplier qualification, quality agreements, contract negotiations, and change order and budget management.
* Clinical supply chain experience, including forecasting, inventory planning, IRT/RTSM, and GMP packaging oversight.
* Experience in both small biotech (self-driven, requiring problem solving and flexibility) and larger biopharma (more structured training and processes).

existing_roles.description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE), supporting Blue Origin’s mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. The team fosters innovation and drives engineering workflows of the future, shared solutions and standards, simplicity and lower costs, and manufacturable design.

**About the Program**
---------------------

Project Sunrise is designing and building orbital data centers — spacecraft that run AI compute workloads on 100% solar power in orbit. This is a first-of-kind program at the intersection of spacecraft engineering and hyperscale GPU infrastructure, housed within Blue Origin. We are building the team from scratch and need people who can operate at the frontier of both domains.

  

**About the Role**
------------------

his is a leadership role with technical depth: you will manage and develop people, and also own integration and test technical content yourself, alongside senior individual contributors who report to you. You have led spacecraft integration and test through qualification and into production, and you want to do it again with a new kind of payload, a tighter schedule, and a team you get to shape from the start. You will work side by side with Manufacturing, Systems Engineering (verification), the technical leads for the spacecraft bus, compute system, software, and operations. You will represent Assembly, Integration & Test in Program leadership forums and reviews.

  

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Build and lead the Assembly, Integration & Test organization: hire and develop integration and test engineers, technicians, and automation and test data specialists, set clear ownership, and scale the team as the program moves from qualification to production

* Own the integration and test schedule and facility resource allocation: sequence qualification and acceptance campaigns, balance competing demands for chambers, shakers, and test benches, and surface schedule risk early

* Own test anomaly resolution: set the process for stopping safely, preserving evidence, finding root cause, and dispositioning nonconformances, and close anomalies with the design and systems teams

* Plan facilities and equipment: define the space, power, cleanroom, environmental test, and ground support equipment needs, and make build, buy, or lease decisions on schedule

* Drive the design the production flow from first-article integration through repeatable acceptance, with defined stations, handoffs, and test gates that Manufacturing and Operations can run

* Drive test automation: set the architecture for electrical ground support and automated test equipment, and deliver more than 80% automated acceptance testing

* Own the test data and digital thread: make sure results are captured, stored, and traceable to requirements, configuration, and hardware serial numbers, and that they flow to engineering, quality, and operations

* Work with Systems Engineering to implement the verification plan: make sure test configurations, procedures, and readiness reviews support requirement closure, and give test feasibility feedback into requirements and design

* Partner with the spacecraft bus, compute system, and software teams so designs can be integrated and tested, building test access, telemetry, and interface needs into the design early

* Manage relationships with suppliers and external test houses: define scope, schedule, and acceptance criteria, and bring the program's integration and test standards to supplier reviews

* Support the production readiness maturity checklist with objective evidence from integration and test

* Set the safety culture on the factory floor and in the test cell, including hazardous operations review and safe handling, and build a team that stops work without hesitation when something looks wrong

  

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or a related technical field; master's degree preferred

* 12+ years of spacecraft integration and test, or comparably complex hardware test, experience, including ownership of spacecraft-level qualification or acceptance testing

* Prior experience leading and developing engineers and technicians as a manager, lead, or chief test engineer

* Demonstrated experience running a test schedule and test facilities for flight hardware, including environmental test (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMI/EMC) and the resource trade-offs that come with it

* Experience resolving test anomalies and nonconformances on flight hardware through root cause and closure

* Experience with test automation, including electrical ground support equipment and automated test equipment, and with test data management and traceability

* Experience establishing or substantially improving integration and test processes, facilities, or tools in a fast-moving environment

* Ability to make and defend sound technical decisions with incomplete information, and to communicate clearly with engineers, executives, suppliers, and customers

  

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience taking a spacecraft from first-article integration to production-rate acceptance testing, including converting manual procedures to automated test

* Experience with high-power or high-heat-flux spacecraft, or with high-density electronics, HPC, or GPU hardware in demanding environments

* Experience planning and commissioning new test facilities or major environmental test equipment

* Experience managing external test houses or test suppliers, including scope, schedule, and quality oversight

* Hands-on experience with digital engineering and manufacturing execution or test data systems, including linking test results to configuration and requirements

* Experience on commercial or rapid-development programs, and judgment in tailoring heritage standards to what a program actually needs

* Experience supporting launch site operations or on-orbit commissioning

  

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

* U.S. citizenship or permanent residency required (ITAR)

* Travel may be required up to 15% of the time but may change based on project needs.

* Relocation assistance available.

existing_roles.description:
**Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality**

**Location:** Lakewood, Ohio  
**Company:** Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company  
**Employment Type:** Full Time  
**Reports To:** President

**About Ferry Cap**

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is a long-established American manufacturer of engineered fasteners and specialty metal components serving demanding industrial and power generation applications. As we invest in our people, equipment, and operating systems, we are seeking a senior quality leader who can help strengthen our processes and build a companywide culture of quality.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will lead Ferry Cap’s quality organization and serve as a key member of the company’s leadership team.

This is a hands on leadership position for someone with strong experience in metallurgy, metal transformation, manufacturing processes, and heat treatment. The successful candidate will work closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, supply chain, and customers to improve process control, solve technical problems, and ensure consistent product quality.

The right leader will view quality as an operating partnership, not simply an inspection function. This individual must be comfortable working on the production floor, engaging directly with employees, and helping build quality into every stage of the manufacturing process.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all quality assurance, quality control, laboratory, inspection, and quality systems activities.
* Partner directly with operations to establish a culture in which safety, delivery, quality, and cost are shared responsibilities.
* Provide technical leadership related to metallurgy, raw materials, metal forming, metal transformation, machining, threading, and heat treatment.
* Oversee metallurgical testing and analysis, including hardness, microstructure, case depth, decarburization, mechanical properties, material certification, and failure analysis.
* Evaluate and improve heat treatment processes, including furnace controls, quenching, tempering, process consistency, and product conformance.
* Strengthen incoming, in process, and final inspection systems to ensure product requirements are consistently achieved.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action activities involving internal defects, customer complaints, supplier issues, and process failures.
* Use structured problem solving methods such as 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and MSA.
* Maintain and continuously improve the company’s quality management system, documentation, procedures, work instructions, and audit processes.
* Ensure compliance with customer requirements, industry standards, specifications, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Lead customer audits, supplier audits, internal audits, and customer quality reviews.
* Build strong working relationships with customer quality and engineering teams.
* Develop meaningful quality metrics, including first pass yield, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality, customer complaints, corrective action effectiveness, and supplier performance.
* Improve material traceability and process control throughout the manufacturing operation.
* Lead supplier quality development and ensure purchased materials and outside processes meet Ferry Cap requirements.
* Develop, coach, and hold accountable the quality team while strengthening quality knowledge throughout the organization.
* Support new product introduction, process changes, capital projects, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish clear containment, escalation, and corrective action processes when quality concerns arise.

**Required Qualifications**

* Significant quality leadership experience in a metal manufacturing environment.
* Strong practical knowledge of metallurgy, material properties, metal transformation, and heat treatment.
* Experience with manufacturing processes such as cold forming, forging, machining, threading, rolling, or similar metalworking operations.
* Demonstrated ability to diagnose metallurgical and manufacturing process failures.
* Experience leading quality systems, customer audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
* Strong working knowledge of dimensional inspection, mechanical testing, metallurgical testing, calibration, and measurement systems.
* Experience using quality tools such as PFMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA, 8D, and root cause analysis.
* Proven ability to work collaboratively with operations and engineering teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem solving skills.
* Willingness to spend significant time on the manufacturing floor and become personally involved in resolving issues.
* Bachelor’s degree in metallurgy, materials science, engineering, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant manufacturing experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including at least five years in a leadership role.
* Experience with engineered fasteners, high strength components, critical industrial products, or power generation applications.
* Experience with ISO based quality management systems and customer specific quality requirements.
* Experience working with commercial heat treat suppliers and internal heat treatment operations.
* ASQ certification, Six Sigma certification, or formal Lean manufacturing training.
* Experience working in a union manufacturing environment.

**Leadership Profile**

The successful candidate will be:

* Hands on and comfortable working directly with production employees.
* Collaborative and capable of building trust across departments.
* Technically strong, practical, and decisive.
* Focused on preventing defects instead of relying on inspection to find them.
* Comfortable challenging existing practices while respecting Ferry Cap’s people and history.
* Able to balance customer requirements with operational realities.
* Committed to accountability, continuous improvement, and developing others.

**Why Join Ferry Cap**

This position offers the opportunity to play a major role in the continued transformation and growth of a historic American manufacturing company. The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will have direct access to company leadership, meaningful influence over operations, and the opportunity to build a quality culture that supports Ferry Cap’s customers, employees, and long term success.

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

At Insmed, every moment and every patient counts — and so does every person who joins in. For patients, for each other, and for the future of science, we’re in. Are you?

  
  

**About the Role:**

Reporting to a Director of Clinical Quality Assurance, the Sr. Manager of Clinical Quality Assurance serves as a Development QA (DevQA) representative on the development team assuring quality and regulatory compliance related to GCPs and other related activities performed by Clinical Study (Trial) Teams. You will provide support and promote collaboration internally and externally to ensure all systems, processes and their outcomes comply with applicable international and national standards, regulations, and guidelines.

**What You'll Do:**

In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to Serve and maintain qualification as a GCP Subject Matter Expert (SME) as well as contribute to and support the maintenance of a risk-based and scientific-based quality system to support GCP. You’ll also:

  

* Ensure that a strategic audit plan is implemented and activities are conducted and reported according to SOPs and regulations.
* Perform audits of investigator sites, TMFs, vendors, and internal systems/processes.

* Support strategic direction with cross functional working groups to identify and mitigate GCP quality and compliance issues.
* Establish and foster compliance with ICH E6 Guideline for Good Clinical Practice.
* Provide support and coaching to other staff members to develop additional quality and auditing resources.
* Manage quality documentation in Veeva QMS.
* Act as company’s representative during regulatory agency inspections.

**Who You Are:**

**Basic Qualifications**

You meet the following minimum education and experience requirements:

* BA/BS degree in Biology or Chemistry or related life sciences discipline along with a minimum of 5 years of GCP experience.
  

**Preferred Qualifications**

In addition to meeting the basic qualifications above, you will also possess some or all of the following:

* An understanding and practical working knowledge of clinical regulations, good clinical practices, development processes, and regulatory inspection procedures.
* Experience in developing SOPs, reviewing internal clinical, regulatory, and medical processes to ensure they are consistent with current regulatory and GCP requirements.

* Highly organized with a strong attention to detail, clarity, accuracy, and conciseness.

This is a fully remote role. It can be performed effectively from anywhere while staying connected to your Insmed team and community. Occasional travel for team meetings or events may be expected.

This position involves frequent domestic/international travel (up to 25-30%) to support clinical QA including external audits.

GCC is a world-class company that produces, distributes and markets cement, ready-mixed concrete, aggregates, and innovative products related to the construction industries in Mexico and the United States. We take pride in being a market leader with a culture of innovation, high performance and safety. GCC offers a very competitive benefits program including paid time off, medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability insurance plans, and a 401K.
  
  
**What you will do:**  
Directs, coordinates and administers all production, quality control, maintenance, engineering, purchasing and process control activities required in meeting the operations budget objectives and maintains alignment with the strategic plans of GCCA for the preservation of the plant's physical assets and to meet projected sales goals. Directs and coordinates activities to obtain optimum efficiency and economy of operations and maximize profits by performing the following duties personally or through subordinate managers and supervisors.
  
  

* Responsible for planning, directing, organizing and scheduling all manufacturing and quality control activities for the effective operation of the plant.
* Plans and direct the plant machinery and mobile equipment preventive maintenance program and all major maintenance projects and activities.
* Plans and directs the expenditures of the capital program.
* Directs the engineering program involving technical support to production and maintenance, operational cost studies, construction and environmental controls.
* Conducts final reviews of and approves all plant budget forecasts, standards, staffing schedules and capital programs.
* Directs the inventory control of all materials, parts and supplies needed to support the operational activities.

* Develops long-range plans for plant operations, capital programs, and raw material reserves and personnel requirements.
* Establishes performance standards for the operational departments including all cost and man-hour standards; policy governing control of product quality standards; the maintenance, repairs and construction budgets; and the necessary quantity and quality levels of all raw materials and fuels used by the plant.
* Hires, counsels, and trains assigned personnel, set individual goals, evaluates performance, recommends salary adjustments, promotion or transfer, approves time-off, and accomplishes objectives through the qualities of strong leadership.
* Directs the efforts to maintain compliance with all city, county, state and federal regulations; maintains a cordial working relationship with the surrounding community.

* Coordinates activities of departments such as operating, quality control, engineering, and maintenance with GCCA planning, sales, process, or research and development, to effect operational efficiency and economy.

* Confers with administrative personnel and reviews activity, operating, and sales reports to determine changes in programs or operations required.
* Promotes organization in industry, manufacturing or trade associations, Chamber of Commerce and community charities and agencies.

* Bachelor’s Degree in Chemical, Mechanical, or Electromechanical Engineering.
* Master’s in Business Administration.
* Ten years’ experience in cement processes and business practices in the cement industry as well as ten years’ experience in maintenance, production, and quality control management.

existing_roles.title: Director of Operations
existing_roles.description:
Description:

**Job Title:** Director of Campus Operations

**Department:** Facilities

**Reports To:** Executive Director of Administration

**Direct Reports:** Assistant Director of Campus Operations

**FLSA Status:** Exempt

**Prepared By:** Human Resources

**Prepared Date:** November 11, 2026

**OUR MISSION**

The mission of Eastern Star Church is to form followers of Jesus to love God, love people, and live to serve. Guided by our vision of Growing People to Love Like Jesus, we are committed to creating environments that support worship, discipleship, community engagement, and service.

**YOUR ROLE IN OUR MISSION**

Under the direction of the Executive Director of Administration, the **Director of Campus Operations** provides strategic leadership, oversight, and accountability for campus operations and facilities across Eastern Star Church and its affiliated organizations, including JEWEL Human Services.

This role is responsible for establishing operational standards, ensuring effective stewardship of facilities and resources, and leading the development and performance of the operations team. Through direct supervision of the Assistant Director of Operations and other assigned leaders, the Director ensures that campus operations are safe, efficient, consistent, and aligned with organizational priorities.

The Director serves as a key partner in advancing the ministry’s mission and strategic plan by ensuring that our facilities and physical environments support worship, discipleship, community outreach, and an exceptional experience for all who enter. The position emphasizes strategic planning, leadership development, financial accountability, and continuous improvement while delegating day-to-day operational execution to the Assistant Director of Operations.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provide strategic leadership, direction, and oversight for campus operations and facilities across Eastern Star Church and its affiliated properties, under the direction of the Executive Director of Administration.
* Establish operational standards and performance expectations to ensure all facilities are safe, functional, well-maintained, and reflective of a culture of excellence and stewardship, holding the Assistant Director of Operations accountable for daily implementation.
* Develop and recommend long-term facilities strategies, including capital improvements, renovations, and expansion planning, in alignment with organizational priorities and the direction of the Executive Director of Administration.
* Provide leadership and oversight for facilities-related capital projects, ensuring appropriate planning, budgeting, resource allocation, and accountability for successful completion within approved timelines and budgets.
* Lead, coach, and develop the Assistant Director of Operations and other assigned direct reports, establishing clear expectations, delegated responsibilities, performance measures, and opportunities for professional growth.
* Establish and maintain consistent operational policies, facility standards, and accountability measures across all campuses and affiliated properties, ensuring effective implementation through the Assistant Director of Operations.
* Partner with executive leadership, Campus Pastors, ministry leaders, and production and creative teams to align campus operations, facility resources, and operational priorities with worship services, programs, events, and organizational needs.
* Provide strategic oversight of vendor relationships, contracts, and service providers, ensuring quality, compliance, cost-effectiveness, and accountability, while delegating routine vendor coordination and service management to the Assistant Director of Operations.
* Develop, manage, and monitor facilities and operations budgets in partnership with Finance and the Executive Director of Administration, ensuring responsible stewardship of resources, financial accountability, and timely identification of budget variances.
* Establish and oversee safety, security, emergency preparedness, and risk management standards, ensuring regulatory compliance and holding operational leadership accountable for implementing and maintaining required procedures.
* Lead the development and continuous improvement of operational systems, processes, technology, and workflows that strengthen efficiency, consistency, communication, and accountability across all campus operations.
* Establish campus experience and operational readiness standards to ensure facilities consistently provide safe, welcoming, functional, and well-prepared environments that support ministry effectiveness and reflect the mission of Eastern Star Church.
* Establish and monitor departmental performance goals and key performance indicators, evaluating operational effectiveness, preventive maintenance performance, campus readiness, service delivery, and resource utilization.
* Provide regular operational reports to the Executive Director of Administration, including departmental performance, budget status, capital project progress, operational risks, and recommendations for continuous improvement.
* Collaborate with the Executive Director of Administration to establish departmental priorities, evaluate organizational needs, recommend resource allocations, and support the implementation of organizational strategic initiatives.
* Carry out all responsibilities with excellence, integrity, trust, professionalism, and the utmost confidentiality.

Perform other duties as assigned

Requirements:

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Demonstrated alignment with the mission, vision, and values of the ministry.
* Proven ability to lead large-scale operations and facilities across multiple sites.
* Strong leadership presence with the ability to influence across departments.
* Active member of Eastern Star Church within three months of starting in the role
* Attend at least one weekly Sunday service.
* Active in a Ministry within three months of starting in the role.
* Complete FFI 101 series or is currently enrolled in class.
* Consistent giver as an opportunity to show God Owns It All by giving back to Him the first of what He gives to us.
* Please refer to the Eastern Star Church Discipleship Policy for additional details.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of leadership experience in operations, facilities, or multi-site management
* Experience leading large-scale projects, capital improvements, renovations, multi-site operations and vendor relationships.
* Strong financial and budget management experience.
* A combination of relevant experience and demonstrated leadership may be considered in place of formal education requirements.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS**

* Relevant facilities, operations, or project management certifications (preferred but not required).

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* This role requires regular travel between multiple campus and organizational locations.
* Must be available to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as required for church services, events, emergencies, and operational needs.
* Work is performed in a combination of office, campus, event, and facilities environments.
* Must be able to stand, walk, climb stairs, inspect facilities, and move throughout campus locations for extended periods of time.
* Must be able to effectively communicate in meetings, public settings, and operational environments.
* Must be able to occasionally lift and transport materials or equipment up to 25 pounds.
* Requires the ability to manage multiple priorities and respond effectively in fast-paced and high-demand environments

existing_roles.title: Director, Commercialization Partnerships Operations
existing_roles.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

**The Opportunity:**

The Director, Commercialization Partnerships and Operationsserves as the primary operational and partnership role at RevMed headquarters supporting the Senior Director, Commercialization Partnerships and Operations This role is responsible for driving operational and partnership excellence, governance structure, financial tracking, and cross-functional alignment across select regional commercialization partners and territory-specific distributors. This role will also partner with regional commercial heads to support relationship management and commercial readiness across the same distribution partner(s).

By serving as the central HQ liaison, this role ensures seamless coordination between RevMed’s internal functional teams (Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Medical Affairs, Finance) and external partners including regional commercial and distribution partners to achieve commercial readiness, regulatory/MAA approval, compliant named-patient access programs, and reliable product supply for a select region.

Core Responsibilities & Scope:

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) & Governance Framework

* Consistent KPI Architecture**:** Establish, standardize, and monitor a unified commercial and operational KPI framework across select region/partner.
* Commercial & Non-Commercial KPIs: Forecast/order accuracy, market access, medical information metrics, performance to volume targets, order-to-cash cycle times, stockout frequency, inventory buffer levels, and lead-time adherence.
* Regulatory & Quality KPIs*:* Variances/amendment submission timelines, adherence to quality and PV agreements.
* Governance & Decision-Making: Operationalize joint governance bodies (e.g., Joint Steering Committees [JSC], Joint Commercial Committees [JCC], and Joint Operations Committees [JOC]) and joint pricing decisions.
* Define escalation pathways, charter guidelines, voting rights, and decision-making matrices (RevMed vs. Partner/Distributor) across commercial, pricing, regulatory, and supply chain domains.

Financial Reporting & Revenue Reconciliation

* Quarterly Financial Tracking: Partner with RevMed HQ Finance and Partner Commercial Operations to track, report, and analyze quarterly commercial revenue, transfer pricing, and royalty/profit-share milestones. Reconcile financial tracking on quarterly basis as necessary.
* KPI-Based Financial Reconciliation: Lead the quarterly financial reconciliation process across partners based on contracted KPIs, volume tiers, milestone achievements, and operational claw backs or bonuses.
* Commercial Dashboard Management: Maintain real-time executive dashboards reporting financial performance, sales volume, inventory valuation, and partner margin compliance.

**Required Skills, Experience and Education:**

* Education: B.S./B.A. in Business, Life Sciences, Supply Chain, or Finance (MBA or advanced degree preferred).
* Experience: 8–12+ years of experience in the biopharmaceutical industry, with direct experience in Alliance Management, Commercial Operations, Strategic Account Operations, or Global Program Management.
* Cross-Functional Expertise: Proven track record bridging commercial activities with technical/operations functions (Supply Chain, Quality/CMC, Regulatory, Medical Affairs, Finance).
* Negotiation Experience: Demonstrated success developing, negotiating, and operationalizing licensing, distribution, commercialization or alliance agreements.
* Geographic & Regional Knowledge**:** Solid understanding of regional pharmaceutical markets, regulatory environments (regional & national competent authorities), pricing & reimbursement dynamics, and distribution models (direct vs. distributor/partner).
* Travel: Ability to travel up to 30%. Hybrid role, at minimum 2-3 days in office at Redwood City headquarters.

**Preferred Skills:**

* Oncology development, supply chain, and commercialization experience.
* Prior experience in a smaller, rapidly growing biotech or pharmaceutical company.

#LI-JW1 #LI-Remote

The range displayed on each job posting is intended to be the base pay salary range for an individual working onsite in Redwood City and will be adjusted for the local market a candidate is based in. Our base pay salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Individual base pay salary is determined by multiple factors, including job-related skills, experience, market dynamics, and relevant education or training.

Please note that base pay salary range is one part of the overall total rewards program at RevMed, which includes competitive cash compensation, robust equity awards, strong benefits, and significant learning and development opportunities.

We will only collect, process and use any personal data that you provide to us in accordance with our CCPA Notice and Privacy Policy. For additional information, please contact privacy@revmed.com.

Base Pay Salary Range

$201,000 - $251,000 USD

existing_roles.title: Regional Director of Operations
existing_roles.description:
Advance your career as a Regional Director of Operations (CDM - Certified Dietary Manager) in Illinois, supporting environmental services and food service operations within our healthcare facilities. If you're passionate about mentoring teams and driving excellence across multiple locations, we invite you to apply today.

**As a Regional Director of Operations - Dietary and Environmental Services, you will...** Oversee all assigned facilities, ensuring leadership and guidance in operations, finances, human resources and client relationships, while providing direct supervision to the facility Food Service Directors and Environmental Services Directors. **Must live in the state of Illinois and have previous Healthcare Dietary experience.**

***Key Responsibilities:***

* Actively support and apply all company and facility policies and procedures to ensure the highest quality of service is being provided to our customers at the lowest possible cost.
* Work with Corporate and/or onsite dietitians to ensure that all federal and state requirements are being achieved.
* Cultivate and maintain business partnerships with clients by developing a broad knowledge and understanding of clients’ and their customers’ needs and expectations, including:
* Establish and maintain internal Quality Assurance and Assessment processes in each assigned facility, including inspections, annual client satisfaction surveys, keep the company and its facilities on the cutting edge of our industry.
* Actively participate in food service-related committees within assigned facilities (if applicable), or otherwise be involved in and visible at special events within each assigned facility, to demonstrate the company’s team approach and commitment to the clients
* Plan and develop each unit’s operational budgets and demonstrate an understanding of the company’s financial objectives for each unit. Financial responsibilities include:
* Review financial results weekly and monthly and make necessary adjustments to improve operational performance.
* Develop a weekly financial plan to include sales, menu and production records, food purchases, inventory, and labor productivity to assist each unit in achieving its budget targets.
* Educate Food Service Directors and Environmental Service Directors for each facility in P&L process (where applicable) and review month-end results for each facility.
* Ensure all established accounting practices and timelines are consistently adhered to.
* Provides assistance as needed, with new business bids, rebids for current clients/customers, and the development of new programs, including:
* Renegotiate contract terms and/or fee/pricing increases with client, when necessary.
* Manage transition of new business accounts.
* Conduct audits and evaluate each facility’s performance in the areas of food production, menu and recipe standards, sanitation, uniforms, purchasing, inventories, safety, payroll, human resources compliance and record keeping.
* Demonstrate working knowledge of operational, accounting and human resources policies and procedures (i.e. new hire process, payroll, etc.).
* Ensure all human resources and safety practices and policies are intact and adhered to.
* Hold facility Directors and employees accountable for behavior and performance, following Corrective Action guidelines when necessary.
* Conduct training and development needs assessment of Food Service Directors and arrange necessary training, including the areas of food and cost productions, customer services, team building, time management, human resources skills, etc.
* Communicate with and assist in developing goals and objectives for each Food Service Director. Meet with Directors on an individual basis to assess goals and areas of opportunity.
* Support Directors in conducting training and development needs assessment of employees and assist in arranging appropriate training sessions/tools.
* Ensure companies systems are followed and in compliance daily

**Regional Food Service Director Minimum Requirements:**

* High School diploma (required)
* Certified Dietary Manager (required)
* Multi-site Dietary Operations experience (required)
* Ability to travel within your region frequently (required)
* Minimum 2-5 years’ experience coordinating food service operations
* Bachelor’s degree in culinary arts or related field (preferred, but not required)
* Demonstrated ability to lead and guide teams.
* Strong initiative.
* Strong ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality of records and information.
* Skill in the use of operating basic office equipment.

**Why Join Our Team?**

Whether you’re looking for a **challenge or opportunity for growth as a Certified Dietary Manager** this provides the chance to build your leadership skills in the Healthcare Dietary sector in Environmental Services and Dietary operations, while doing work that truly matters!

existing_roles.description:
**VP of Production**
--------------------

**Location:** Los Angeles, Detroit, or San Francisco  
**Employment:** Full time, in person  
**Base salary:** $200,000–$350,000 annually

American factories deserve a supply chain that moves as fast as they do. Nox Metals is building it, along with the tools that run it. We’re a technology company supplying raw metal to frontier American manufacturers. We use software and automation to supply metal to factories faster than the industry thought possible.

### **The role**

We’re hiring a VP of Production to lead manufacturing performance across Nox Metals’ facilities. You will own how work moves through our factories: production planning, daily execution, capacity, staffing, quality, productivity, and on-time delivery.

This is a hands-on manufacturing leadership role with real time on the factory floor. You will develop production leaders, resolve constraints, and create repeatable ways of working that help teams deliver as demand grows. Success means safe, reliable production and clear accountability from the daily schedule through completed customer orders.

### **You will**

* Lead production execution across facilities, with clear expectations for safety, quality, output, cost, and delivery.
* Translate demand into practical production, staffing, shift, and capacity plans.
* Develop plant and production leaders who take ownership of results and build strong teams.
* Establish daily operating reviews, shift handoffs, escalation paths, and performance measures that drive action.
* Identify bottlenecks, reduce downtime and rework, and improve material flow and labor productivity.
* Build consistent training, work instructions, and qualification standards while staying close to how work happens.
* Protect material traceability and quality throughout production.
* Partner with maintenance and engineering on equipment reliability, capacity improvements, and automation.
* Work with supply chain and commercial teams to align material availability, production commitments, and customer needs.
* Partner with finance on production economics and equipment investment decisions.
* Help new or expanded facilities establish reliable production and sustain performance as they ramp.

### **You are**

* A manufacturing leader with a record of improving factory performance and developing accountable leaders.
* Experienced managing production teams, schedules, equipment constraints, and competing priorities.
* Uncompromising about safety, quality, and traceability.
* Fluent in capacity, throughput, labor productivity, downtime, and delivery performance.
* Comfortable making decisions on the floor and following through until problems are resolved.
* Practical, direct, and interested in improving manufacturing with software and automation.

### **Nice to have**

Experience leading multiple facilities, scaling production through rapid growth, or working in metals, machining, aerospace, industrial distribution, or related environments.

Expect regular time at our manufacturing facilities and travel between sites as needed.

Nox Metals is an equal opportunity employer. We hire based on skill, attitude, and fit for the work, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, height, weight, marital status, or any other protected status under federal, state, or local law.

We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, and the California Fair Chance Act.

Compensation Range: $200K - $350K

protected_roles.description:
**Overview**
Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger
  
  
The Quality Director plays a pivotal role in leading and strengthening operational quality and quality compliance within a large-scale contract manufacturing facility. Responsible for both Product Quality and Quality Management System (QMS) compliance, this leader ensures quality operations within the manufacturing environment consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business expectations.
  
  
This individual combines strategic vision with hands-on operational quality leadership, ensuring Resonetics delivers world-class quality in a fast-paced, highly regulated medical device manufacturing environment. The role demands proven experience within manufacturing operations, deep expertise in ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820, mastery of advanced quality assurance techniques, and the ability to align and elevate quality performance across multiple value streams.
  
  
Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Quality Leadership**

* Own and lead all aspects of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational processes deliver consistent, compliant, and high-yield outcomes.
* Partner closely with Operations leadership to embed quality into daily production activities and drive problem-solving directly on the manufacturing floor.
* Implement and oversee statistical process control (SPC), process capability, and other data-driven tools to ensure process stability and continuous improvement.
* Monitor and manage critical quality metrics, taking immediate action to address gaps and prevent recurrence of issues.
* Oversee validation strategies (IQ/OQ/PQ) for manufacturing processes and equipment, ensuring robustness and compliance.
* Provide quality leadership in New Product Introduction (NPI), ensuring robust process validation, risk management, and seamless transition from development into full-scale manufacturing.

**Quality Systems & Compliance**

* Ensure the ISO-certified QMS is operationally effective within manufacturing sites and continuously improved to support business growth.
* Maintain full compliance with ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, and other relevant standards through proactive system management and audit readiness.

**Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving**

* Lead root cause investigations and corrective actions for complex production challenges.
* Drive Lean and Six Sigma initiatives that enhance manufacturing efficiency while strengthening compliance and product quality.
* Share best practices across sites to ensure standardization and scalability of quality improvements.

**Customer & Supplier Interface**

* Serve as the primary quality leader for high-visibility customers, ensuring confidence in Resonetics’ ability to deliver consistently high-quality products.
* Lead the supplier quality program, ensuring raw materials and outsourced processes meet stringent requirements to support operational excellence.

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Build and mentor a strong quality team embedded within the manufacturing organization.
* Provide training in advanced quality tools (Gage R&R, SPC, pFMEA, Risk Analysis, Validation, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA) to elevate operational capability.
* Foster a culture of quality culture and ownership on the production floor, engaging all levels of the workforce.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 7 years’ experience in a Medical Device Quality Management role.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Demonstrated background in an ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820 quality management system.
* Strong communication skills (verbal and writing)
* BS degree in a management or engineering discipline
* Experience hosting FDA inspections and ISO audits

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience in a technical, regulated environment.
* Experience with finished medical device assembly and oversight of sterilization
* Experience with Quality Management Software (eQMS) and ERP systems
* Certified Quality Auditor

**Physical Demands**

* Light office work, approximately 25%+ travel

**Compensation**
The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000.00 - $222,000.00.
  
  
For temp, temp-to-hire, and regular full-time positions, our company policy is that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must already be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

**Obsessed by Science. Entrepreneurial by Nature. United by Purpose.**
Diasorin is a global leader in immunodiagnostic and molecular diagnostic solutions, advancing science to improve patient outcomes worldwide. For more than 50 years, we have combined scientific rigor with an entrepreneurial mindset, operating with a strong commitment to innovation, accountability, and results to deliver trusted diagnostic solutions.
  
  
As the Diagnostics Specialist, Diasorin continuously invests in research, technology, and people. Guided by our values of operational excellence, customer focus, and teamwork, we empower teams to think boldly, act decisively, and transform ideas into meaningful impact across one of the industry’s broadest specialty diagnostic portfolios.
  
  
When you join Diasorin, you are not just filling a role. You are helping build what comes next.
  
  
**Why Join Diasorin**

* Build What Matters Take ownership, challenge the status quo, and contribute directly to solutions that improve patient care worldwide.
* Innovate with Agility at a Global Scale Work in an entrepreneurial environment that enables speed, collaboration, and global impact.
* Grow in a People-Centered Culture Thrive in a culture that values accountability, inclusion, and continuous development.

**Job Scope:**
The Director, Quality Assurance for Austin will lead, establish, implement and maintain quality assurance systems and activities ensuring compliance with domestic and international quality system standards and regulations for commercial medical devices designed, produced and marketed by Luminex. Partner with Manufacturing, Design/Development, Systems Engineering, Quality Control and others across functions to deliver the highest quality instruments, and reagents. This position is responsible for the oversight, control and release of instruments and reagents, quality organizational management, budget preparation, personnel management, organizational goals and metrics, and Executive Level presentations. The Director, Quality Assurance for Austin is a leader and a mentor.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities And Duties**

* Ensures that the Austin site demonstrates regulatory compliance per GLP/GCP/cGMP/GXP, ISO, and other applicable regulations.
* Support instrument new product development and manufacturing changes, provides guidance to the core teams and participate in the process.
* Leader in process optimization by Identifying and analyzing opportunities for continual improvements in product/service quality, customer satisfaction, and company profitability.
* Leads the strategy and improvements for the manufacturing and service depot of Instruments for our customers and partners in compliance with regulations and standards.
* Participates and manage activities for external audits such as ISO, FDA or other regulatory bodies for the Austin site. Acts in Audits - as co-host, SME or escort
* Responds to alleged QMS violations of regulations, policies, procedures as the result of both external and external audits by evaluating and recommending the initiation of investigative activities, immediate corrections and risk analysis processes. Coordinates responses to external audits and manages corrective actions to close.
* Interacts with various internal and external groups to facilitate the completion of internal audits, handling of non-conformances, performing Risk Assessments, CAPA, investigation and support, manufacturing validation as well as Design Transfer.
* QMS improvements and enhancements and is a leading member of the Quality Management Team. Works across the corporation to align and define quality approach for molecular diagnostic products.
* Partners with Site Leadership and Field Quality to conduct, manage, and evaluate investigations related to customer complaints, nonconformances, audits, corrective/preventive action concerns, deviations, recalls, and potential injuries
* Appropriately escalate Quality issues to the Vice President Quality Assurance Molecular Division
* Provide leadership in the application of Quality Tools such as Risk Management, Root Cause Investigations, Designs of Experiments, Capability Studies, in the establishment and investigation of process and products failures and implement lasting solutions of such failures.
* May act as IVDR Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) for Luminex sites to ensure: the conformity of the devices is appropriately checked before a device is released, the post-market surveillance and reporting obligations are fulfilled and all requirements established between Luminex and Authorized representative are met.
* May act as Management Representative for the site. In this capacity, ensure that product meets label claims and customer satisfaction, any quality or regulatory issue is elevated to the President and/or Vice President Quality Assurance Compliance North America and oversee and drive continuous improvement.
* Develops and releases Change Plans and actions to support the changing needs and requirements of the organization as the result of strategic changes in business direction
* Provide other Quality related technical training as necessary
* Directs activities of employees or through managers who exercise full supervision for daily operations. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws.
* Maintains talent through recruiting and development opportunities. Continually develops internal candidates through succession planning and career development.
* Responsible for enforcing all EHS policies in their span of control
* Be part of any the new key and strategic projects and due diligence process if required
* Ensure all site-level activities and related documentation are aligned with corporate procedures and conducted in accordance with DiaSorin’s established Corporate and Quality Assurance governance requirements.

**Education, Experience And Qualifications**

* Minimum Bachelor degree in a science or engineering discipline with 8+ years of relevant experience/training
* 10+ Years of Experience in Quality Assurance or Regulatory Affairs activities in a cGMP Medical Device or Pharmaceutical environment
* 5+ years of Demonstrated knowledge of current industry quality practices under ISO 13485, ISO 14971, CFR 820 and CFR 806 and international regulations preferred
* 2+ years of Management experience in a complex quality assurance/quality systems field
* 2+ years of Ability to provide leadership to others in the organization through influence, innovative practices and coaching skills to foster a corporate culture of responsiveness, compliance awareness, self-regulation, quality system ownership, challenge of status quo, and continuous improvement in order to achieve the highest level of compliance.
* 5+ years of Excellent problem solving methodology, using industry accepted concepts and tools to solve complex problems in creative and effective ways as they apply to compliance issues.
* 5+ years of Hands-on ability to sort through technical complexities and work in a flexible changing environment.
* 5+ years of Possesses a strong scientific and technical background, sufficient to establish creditability with senior management as well as the manufacturing and product development teams.
* Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills
* Thorough knowledge of standards and regulations (cGMP, ISO 13485)
* Highly organized with proven time management and prioritization skills
* Ability to work independently and with minimal supervision
* High degree of problem solving, attention to detail, and analytical skills.
* Experience working independently in a fast-paced environment with rapidly changing priorities
* Ability to handle the pressure of meeting tight deadlines

**What We Offer**
Diasorin offers a competitive rewards package focused on your overall well-being. We are proud to offer a comprehensive plan of health benefits, retirement and financial wellbeing, time off programs, wellbeing support and perks. Benefits may vary by role, country, region, union status, and other employment status factors. You may also be eligible to participate in an annual incentive program. An incentive award, if any, depends on various factors, including, individual and organizational performance.
